[Unending Itch](/Equipment.aspx?ID=4551)
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Alchemical" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=6" />
<trait label="Consumable" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=36" />
<trait label="Injury" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=97" />
<trait label="Poison" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=126" />
<trait label="Virulent" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=162" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Treasure Vault](/Sources.aspx?ID=320) pg. 71

**Price** 700 gp

<row gap="medium">

**Usage** held in 2 hands

**Bulk** L
</row>

<row gap="medium">
<row gap="tiny"><row>**Activate**</row><actions string="Two Actions" /><row>Interact</row></row>

 

 

 
</row>

</column>

---

Invented to cause a lengthy and unpleasant demise, this poison manifests as an itch that can’t be soothed. The victim experiences the poison damage as irritation rather than pain or sickness and must succeed at a DC 34 [Perception](/Rules.aspx?ID=2040) check to realize they’re poisoned. The poison can also be identified with a DC 34 [Medicine](/Skills.aspx?ID=42) check. Once the victim has lost half or more of its Hit Points, the DC drops to 30 for either check. As long as the victim doesn’t realize it’s poisoned, the GM makes its saving throws in secret.

**Saving Throw** DC 34 Fortitude (secret); **Maximum Duration** 5 minutes; **Stages 1–5** 1d6 poison damage (1 round)

</column>

<traits>

<row gap="medium">

</row>

---

You cease aging, and if you were older than young adult in age, you become a young adult again. You gain a +4 status bonus to saves against [death](/Traits.aspx?ID=40) effects and resistance to negative damage equal to half your level. Once per day, from any distance, Abrogail Thrune II can recite a mandatory appearance clause in your Thrune contract as a 3-action activity to summon you to her side, where you are [controlled](/Conditions.aspx?ID=6) by Abrogail for 1 minute before you return.

**Activate** <actions string="Two Actions" /> command;  **Frequency** once per day;   **Effect** You recite a hold harmless provision from your Thrune contract. Reduce your [doomed](/Conditions.aspx?ID=9) value to 0. Abrogail Thrune II is immediately made aware that you have used this ability.

</column>

[Unexceptional](/Equipment.aspx?ID=2563)
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Uncommon" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=159" />
<trait label="Illusion" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=92" />
<trait label="Magical" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=103" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Highhelm](/Sources.aspx?ID=204) pg. 87

**Price** 60 gp

<row gap="medium">

**Usage** applied to an item of light Bulk or less that is no larger than 5 feet by 5 feet by 5 feet

</row>

<row gap="medium">

 

 

 
</row>

</column>

---

Merchants traveling into Stonebreach sometimes apply this accessory rune to specific wares to avoid the notice of thieves. Conversely, many thieves in Highhelm apply these runes to stolen goods to help them smuggle items out of the city. The item gains the effects of [_magic aura_](/Spells.aspx?ID=178) to appear as non-magical. The rune's effects also cause anyone who closely observes or holds the item to believe it is a mundane version of that type of item, such as believing a magical [dagger](/Weapons.aspx?ID=3) to be an ordinary dagger, unless the creature succeeds at a DC 18 Will save. Creatures that succeed their save see that there is more to the item than meets the eye, but aren't immediately aware of the _magic aura_ effect.

<title
    level="1"
    right="Item 15"
    pfs="Restricted"
>
[Unfathomable Stargazer](/Equipment.aspx?ID=2391)
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Rare" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=137" />
<trait label="Cursed" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=274" />
<trait label="Magical" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=103" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Treasure Vault (Remastered)](/Sources.aspx?ID=191) pg. 193

<row gap="medium">

**Usage** held in 1 hand

**Bulk** 1
</row>

<row gap="medium">

 

 

 
</row>

</column>

---

An _unfathomable stargazer_ is a handheld brass telescope etched with constellations, the patterns of which form bizarre, shifting runes. You can observe the night sky with an _unfathomable stargazer_, however, the constellations you glimpse through the telescope distort with expanding and contracting fields of darkness among them. You use [Occultism](/Skills.aspx?ID=11) instead of Perception or [Astronomy Lore](/Skills.aspx?ID=8) when observing the skies with this item, and gain a +2 item bonus on all checks to do so. Once you use it, it fuses to you, and you must succeed at a DC 35 Will save to use another device to observe the stars, including your naked eyes. The telescope imposes a –4 circumstance penalty to [Survival](/Skills.aspx?ID=16) checks to [Sense Direction](/Actions.aspx?ID=64) or navigate. If you critically fail this Survival check, you're subjected to [_warp mind_](/Spells.aspx?ID=369) (DC 34) as you glimpse something horrifying and alien amid the darkness.

<column gap="tiny">

</column>

fields.markdown:
<title
    level="1"
    right="Item 7"
    pfs="Limited"
>
[Unfolding Tree House](/Equipment.aspx?ID=3626)
</title>

<spoilers>May contain spoilers from Wardens of Wildwood</spoilers>

<traits>
<trait label="Uncommon" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=159" />
<trait label="Magical" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=103" />
<trait label="Structure" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=153" />
<trait label="Wood" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=508" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Pathfinder #203 Shepherd of Decay](/Sources.aspx?ID=243) pg. 78

**Price** 340 gp

<row gap="medium">

**Bulk**  L (when not activated)
</row>

<row gap="medium">

 

 

 
</row>

</column>

---

Though it looks like a simple profile of a bird’s wing and body carved into a flat triangle of wood, this magical object can transform into a tree house. 

**Activate—Unfold** <actions string="" /> 1 minute ([concentrate](/Traits.aspx?ID=561), [manipulate](/Traits.aspx?ID=645)) **Frequency** once per day;   **Effect** You unfold the triangle on near-invisible seams and the bird animates, flying up to perch in a tree you designate within 300 feet of you. The bird’s perch can be as high as 200 feet off the ground or the top of the trees, whichever is lower. The bird then alights, expands, and reshapes into an elegantly crafted tree house over the course of 10 minutes. Unlike typical items with the [structure](/Traits.aspx?ID=704) trait, this tree house attaches to the tree instead of needing to be on solid ground. 

Once the tree house is in place, a ladder made of intricately woven vines attached to the tree house unfurls all the way to the ground. It can be manually pulled up by inhabitants of the tree house for safety. The tree house has a small veranda, circular windows, a door with a simple lock, and six bedrolls inside. Atop a small cushion sits a wooden whistle. 

As an action, you can blow the whistle to create a soft bird call. At this signal, the tree house gradually folds back into a bird over the course of 1 minute, gently ejecting any occupants toward the ladder. Afterward, the bird flies to you, seizes the whistle, and then folds back into the wooden triangle. Unless commanded to dismantle, the tree house stays in place indefinitely, though it’s subject to normal wear and damage.

<column gap="tiny">

</column>

<column gap="tiny">

<row gap="medium">

---

Crafted from black iron, this crude suit of _+2 [resilient](/Equipment.aspx?ID=2786) [full plate](/Armor.aspx?ID=50)_ is designed to make you look like a horned demon with your face peering out of the screaming maw of the beast. 

While wearing the armor, you can attack with the helmet's horns. They're a martial melee weapon with the effects of a _+2 [weapon potency rune](/Equipment.aspx?ID=2830)_. They deal 2d8 piercing damage and have the [deadly](/Traits.aspx?ID=570) d12 and [unholy](/Traits.aspx?ID=521) traits. On a critical hit with the horns, the target must succeed at a DC 30 Fortitude or become [drained](/Conditions.aspx?ID=68) 1 (or drained 2 on a critical failure). The horns can't be etched with any runes.

 If you're [holy](/Traits.aspx?ID=517), you're drained 2 and can't recover from this condition while wearing unholy plate. 

**Activate—Demonic Slip** <actions string="Two Actions" /> ([concentrate](/Traits.aspx?ID=561)) **Frequency** once per day;   **Effect** You cast [_translocate_](/Spells.aspx?ID=1724).

**Craft Requirements** You’re unholy; supply one casting of [_translocate_](/Spells.aspx?ID=1724).

>
[Unholy Skill](/Equipment.aspx?ID=5236)
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Rare" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=683" />
<trait label="Contract" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=329" />
<trait label="Invested" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=637" />
<trait label="Magical" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=644" />
<trait label="Teleportation" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=710" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Cheliax, Infernal Inheritence](/Sources.aspx?ID=372) pg. 80

_[**PFS Note**](/pathfinder-society) Pathfinder Society agents should not strike deals with devils without Decemvirate approval._

<row gap="medium">

</row>

<row gap="medium">

 

 

 
</row>

</column>

---

Whether because of a lack of talent or a desire for fame, you've bargained for infernal aid. When you gain this contract, choose a skill. You gain a +2 item bonus to checks with that skill. Once per week, at any distance, the devil who holds your _bargained contract_ can cite a royalties clause, taking from you the amount of currency you'd gain from [Earning Income](/Actions.aspx?ID=2364) on an expert-rank task of your level. The currency teleports directly from your possessions to the devil's vaults. If you're unable to pay, the devil instead takes the item with a value higher than, but closest to, the amount you owe from your possessions as collateral, returning it when you pay the required amount. 

**Activate—Reasonable Force** <actions string="Two Actions" /> ([concentrate](/Traits.aspx?ID=561), [manipulate](/Traits.aspx?ID=645)) **Frequency** once per day;   **Effect** You cite a right of self-defense article in your contract. The contract casts _[diabolical mantle](/Spells.aspx?ID=2929)_, and you can then [Shove](/Actions.aspx?ID=2380) or [Demoralize](/Actions.aspx?ID=2395) an adjacent creature.

<column gap="tiny">

</column>

---

These tattoos were first created using designs and techniques from the seven Shoanti clans. Each clan is known for one tattoo in particular. The clans would seal alliances in ancient days by tattooing their emblems on members of other clans to symbolically share their gifts. Though these tattoos are respected, the clans reserve their most prestigious symbols for true members of the clan.

The tattoo allows you to understand and speak [Shoanti](/Languages.aspx?ID=171). If you already know that language, you instead gain a +1 item bonus on [Diplomacy](/Skills.aspx?ID=39) checks you make when speaking Shoanti to someone who understands it.

**Activate** <actions string="" /> The actions required to Activate the tattoo are the same as those needed to cast its spell;  **Frequency** once per day;   **Effect** The tattoo casts its spell.

<row gap="medium">

---

These tattoos were first created using designs and techniques from the seven Shoanti clans. Each clan is known for one tattoo in particular. The clans would seal alliances in ancient days by tattooing their emblems on members of other clans to symbolically share their gifts. Though these tattoos are respected, the clans reserve their most prestigious symbols for true members of the clan.

The tattoo allows you to understand and speak [Shoanti](/Languages.aspx?ID=171). If you already know that language, you instead gain a +1 item bonus on [Diplomacy](/Skills.aspx?ID=39) checks you make when speaking Shoanti to someone who understands it.

**Activate** <actions string="" /> The actions required to Activate the tattoo are the same as those needed to cast its spell;  **Frequency** once per day;   **Effect** The tattoo casts its spell.

May contain spoilers from Sky King's Tomb **Source** [Pathfinder #193: Mantle of Gold](/Sources.aspx?ID=206) pg. 84 **Usage** worn --- Resembling two hands clasped in friendship, this _[diplomat's badge](/Equipment.aspx?ID=431)_ is designed to be woven into the wearer's braided beard. When the wearer befriends others, one of the hands briefly transforms to resemble the befriended creature's own.
**Forming the Bond** The PCs complete the [rite of repatriation](/Rituals.aspx?ID=105).**Advancing the Bond** Solve problems nonviolently. End ancient grudges and heal old wounds, especially those caused by dwarves.
**Minor Gifts** [ancestors' call](/Relics.aspx?ID=123), [linguistic nexus](/Relics.aspx?ID=49), [repository of knowledge](/Relics.aspx?ID=51) (Dwarf Lore, Genealogy Lore, Warfare Lore)
**Major Gifts** [perception filter](/Relics.aspx?ID=52), or increase the diplomat's badge's item bonus to Diplomacy to +2.

fields.markdown:
**Source** [Character Guide](/Sources.aspx?ID=12) pg. 73 **Usage** worn cloak **Bulk** 1 --- This long, shoddy cloak bears a hood and a simple brass clasp. While wearing the cloak, you gain a +1 item bonus to [Deception](/Skills.aspx?ID=5) checks to Impersonate an individual and to Lie while in character as that individual. **Activate** 1 minute (envision, Interact); **Frequency** once per day; **Requirements** You are Impersonating someone else; **Effect** While conversing or otherwise casually interacting with other creatures, you can adjust the mantle’s clasp to modify those creatures’ recollections of the last 5 minutes of their interaction with you. Each creature must attempt a DC 25 Will save. **Critical Success** The creature recalls the interaction clearly and realizes you were trying to alter their memory.
**Success** The creature recalls the interaction clearly.
**Failure** You decide whether or not the creature recalls the interaction. You can also alter minor details the creature recalls about the interaction, such as the time, place, and whether the interaction was favorable, as determined by the GM.
**Critical Failure** You decide whether or not the creature recalls the interaction. You can also alter major details the creature recalls about the interaction, such as believing you to be another individual or that the creature agreed to a favor, as determined by the GM. Unmemorable Mantle **Source** [Character Guide](/Sources.aspx?ID=12) pg. 73 **Price** 300 gp **Bulk** 1 Unmemorable Mantle (Greater) **Source** [Character Guide](/Sources.aspx?ID=12) pg. 73 **Price** 1,300 gp **Bulk** 1 --- The item bonus is +2, and the Will save DC is 28. Unmemorable Mantle (Major) **Source** [Character Guide](/Sources.aspx?ID=12) pg. 73 **Price** 21,750 gp **Bulk** 1 --- The item bonus is +3, the Will save DC is 38, and you can activate the mantle once every 10 minutes.

fields.text: Item 7+ Unmemorable Mantle Illusion Invested Magical Source Character Guide pg. 73 Usage worn cloak Bulk 1 This long, shoddy cloak bears a hood and a simple brass clasp. While wearing the cloak, you gain a +1 item bonus to Deception checks to Impersonate an individual and to Lie while in character as that individual. Activate 1 minute (envision, Interact); Frequency once per day; Requirements You are Impersonating someone else; Effect While conversing or otherwise casually interacting with other creatures, you can adjust the mantle’s clasp to modify those creatures’ recollections of the last 5 minutes of their interaction with you. Each creature must attempt a DC 25 Will save. Critical Success The creature recalls the interaction clearly and realizes you were trying to alter their memory. Success The creature recalls the interaction clearly. Failure You decide whether or not the creature recalls the interaction. You can also alter minor details the creature recalls about the interaction, such as the time, place, and whether the interaction was favorable, as determined by the GM. Critical Failure You decide whether or not the creature recalls the interaction. You can also alter major details the creature recalls about the interaction, such as believing you to be another individual or that the creature agreed to a favor, as determined by the GM. Item 7 Unmemorable Mantle Source Character Guide pg. 73 Price 300 gp Bulk 1 Item 9 Unmemorable Mantle (Greater) Source Character Guide pg. 73 Price 1,300 gp Bulk 1 The item bonus is +2, and the Will save DC is 28. Item 17 Unmemorable Mantle (Major) Source Character Guide pg. 73 Price 21,750 gp Bulk 1 The item bonus is +3, the Will save DC is 38, and you can activate the mantle once every 10 minutes.

>
[Unnerving](/Equipment.aspx?ID=4997)
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Magical" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=103" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Impossible Magic](/Sources.aspx?ID=355) pg. 205

**Price** 350 gp

<row gap="medium">

**Usage** etched onto armor

</row>

<row gap="medium">

 

 

 
</row>

</column>

---

The sound of weapons clanging against a suit of _unnerving_ armor transforms into an inhuman screech that unsettles enemies and makes them hesitate to attack again. Any creature that hits you with a melee Strike takes a –1 circumstance penalty to its next melee Strike that targets you before the end of your next turn.

<column gap="tiny">

</column>

[Unsullied Blood](/Equipment.aspx?ID=1795)
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Uncommon" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=159" />
<trait label="Catalyst" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=396" />
<trait label="Consumable" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=36" />
<trait label="Magical" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=103" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Impossible Lands](/Sources.aspx?ID=146) pg. 177

<row gap="medium">

**Usage** held in 1 hand

**Bulk** L
</row>

**Access** Characters from Geb have access to this item.

<row gap="medium">
<row gap="tiny"><row>**Activate**</row><actions string="Single Action" /><row>envision</row></row>

 

 

 
</row>

</column>

---

Blood offered from a willing donor was taken directly from the vein and stored in an ornate vial that keeps it as pure and red as the day it was extracted. When this catalyst is added to a [_vampiric touch_](/Spells.aspx?ID=354) spell of up to 4th level, instead of gaining temporary Hit Points based on the damage dealt, you recover half of the damage dealt as Hit Points.

<column gap="tiny">

</column>

---

You can add the catalyst to a _vampiric touch_ spell up to 5th level. In addition to the effects of _lesser unsullied blood_, if the amount of Hit Points that would be restored by the spell exceeds your Hit Point maximum, you gain the excess as temporary Hit Points.

>
[Urn of Ashes](/Equipment.aspx?ID=3420)
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Magical" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=644" />
<trait label="Void" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=510" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Player Core 2](/Sources.aspx?ID=227) pg. 307

**Price** 700 gp

<row gap="medium">

**Usage** held in 1 hand

</row>

<row gap="medium">

 

 

 
</row>

</column>

---

This pewter urn contains the ashes of a benevolent ancestor, with a sliver of lingering spirit that strives to protect you.

**Activate—Doom the Urn** <actions string="Reaction" /> ([concentrate](/Traits.aspx?ID=561))  **Trigger** You would become [doomed](/Conditions.aspx?ID=67), or your doomed value would increase; **Requirements** The ashes aren't doomed;; **Effect** The ashes in the urn intervene, taking the doomed condition in your place, and you don't gain or increase the value of your doomed condition. Each night when you get a full night's rest, you can reduce your own doomed condition or that of the urn, but not both.

**Activate—Spirit's Wrath** <actions string="Single Action" /> ([attack](/Traits.aspx?ID=540), [concentrate](/Traits.aspx?ID=561), [manipulate](/Traits.aspx?ID=645)) **Frequency** once per round;   **Effect** The urn shoots a bolt of void energy at a foe within 30 feet. Attempt a spell attack roll against the target's AC, using a modifier of +15 or your own spell attack modifier, whichever is higher. On a success, the bolt deals 4d4 void damage (doubled on a critical success).

<column gap="tiny">

</column>

---

_Note from Nethys: This item is a constituent part of the [Ursine Avenger Hood](/Archetypes.aspx?ID=200) archetype using the [archetype artifact](/Rules.aspx?ID=1961) rules._

A gift passed from warrior to warrior, this cowl is made from a [cave bear's](/Monsters.aspx?ID=48) skull and fur. Once invested, the wearer gains a +1 item bonus to [Nature](/Skills.aspx?ID=10) checks to [Command an Animal](/Actions.aspx?ID=58), which increases to +2 if the animal is a [bear](/MonsterFamilies.aspx?ID=13). The wearer of the hood feels a constant longing for the wilderness and wild places and takes a –1 item penalty to all [Diplomacy](/Skills.aspx?ID=6) checks to [Gather Information](/Actions.aspx?ID=49) or [Make an Impression](/Actions.aspx?ID=50) if they go more than 5 days inside a large town or city without spending at least 4 hours in the wilderness.

**Destruction** Soak the _Ursine Avenger Hood_ in the blood of a [linnorm](/MonsterFamilies.aspx?ID=69) that is at least 16th level and then burn it in a fire that uses only oak and chrysanthemum as fuel.

---

This round, flat amulet can be made of metal, clay, or leather and is usually highly personalized with runes, sigils, lines of poetry, or a depiction of a storyteller at work. In Azimbye’s case, their gold-rimmed metal amulet boasts fine dwarven workmanship, and bears lines from one of the oldest epic poems of the legendary folk hero Kgalaserke on one side and a stylized portrait of a storytelling event in Ranage’s Circle on the other. While wearing the amulet, you gain a +1 item bonus to Performance checks.

**Activate—Enamoring Story** <actions string="Free Action" /> ([concentrate](/Traits.aspx?ID=32)) **Frequency** once per day; **Trigger** The perfect anecdote or story to impress your interlocutor comes floating to your memory.;  **Effect** You attempt to Make an Impression or Request, using a Performance check instead of a Diplomacy check.

fields.text: Item 5 Uzunjati Storytelling Amulet May contain spoilers from Convocation Rare Invested Magical Source Rival Academies pg. 67 Price 145 gp Usage worn This round, flat amulet can be made of metal, clay, or leather and is usually highly personalized with runes, sigils, lines of poetry, or a depiction of a storyteller at work. In Azimbye’s case, their gold-rimmed metal amulet boasts fine dwarven workmanship, and bears lines from one of the oldest epic poems of the legendary folk hero Kgalaserke on one side and a stylized portrait of a storytelling event in Ranage’s Circle on the other. While wearing the amulet, you gain a +1 item bonus to Performance checks. Activate—Enamoring Story Free Action (concentrate) Frequency once per day; Trigger The perfect anecdote or story to impress your interlocutor comes floating to your memory.; Effect You attempt to Make an Impression or Request, using a Performance check instead of a Diplomacy check.

---

A vaccine grants a creature immunity to a specific strain of disease of a level equal to or less than the vaccine’s level, and a +2 item bonus on all saving throws against other strains of the same disease. For example, a vaccine could grant immunity to putrid plague inflicted by [harpies](/Monsters.aspx?ID=3046) but would only grant a +2 bonus against putrid plague inflicted by a [giant rat](/Monsters.aspx?ID=3162).

**Special** A vaccine is the same rarity as the disease it’s designed to prevent, or as the creature who inflicts the disease if the disease itself doesn’t list a rarity.

**Craft Requirements** Creating a vaccine requires a sample of the disease in question.

>
[Vagabond's Teapot](/Equipment.aspx?ID=4948)
</title>

<spoilers>May contain spoilers from Troubles in Grayce</spoilers>

<traits>
<trait label="Uncommon" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=721" />
<trait label="Magical" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=644" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Troubles in Grayce](/Sources.aspx?ID=327) pg. 118

**Price** 50 gp

<row gap="medium">

**Usage** held in 1 hand

**Bulk** L
</row>

<row gap="medium">

 

 

 
</row>

</column>

---

These ceramic teapots are highly valued by travelers. While the teapot is filled with water, a creature can use a single action with the [concentrate](/Traits.aspx?ID=561) trait to instantly heat the water to boiling, at which point the kettle whistles and the water inside begins to cool at a normal rate. While the water remains heated, it is piping hot, and a creature splashed with it takes 1d4 [nonlethal](/Traits.aspx?ID=661) fire damage. Instead of filling the teapot with water, you can pour an [elixir](/Equipment.aspx?Category=6&Subcategory=8) of 4th level or lower into the pot and use the following activation.

**Activate—Share Brew** <actions string="" /> 10 minutes ([concentrate](/Traits.aspx?ID=561)) **Frequency** once per day;   **Effect** The teapot magically increases the volume of the inserted elixir to produce four uses of the same elixir. Once an elixir has been brewed in the teapot in this way, further attempts that day to brew another elixir spoil the inserted liquid. Any brewed elixir not consumed by the time it cools (typically 10 minutes) loses its alchemical properties.

</column>

_Valorous coins_ are metal disks emblazoned with two crossed swords, with inscriptions exhorting bravery and optimism. The effects of a _valorous coin_ last for 1 hour. During that time, if you’re reduced below a quarter of your Hit Points while wielding the affected weapon, it empowers you with determination and resolve to finish the fight. You gain temporary Hit Points equal to your level that last for 1 minute, and you gain a +1 circumstance bonus to Strikes and damage rolls with the affected weapon for 1 minute. Once this minute ends, so do all effects and the remaining duration of the _valorous coin_, and you’re [fatigued](/Conditions.aspx?ID=73) until you’re healed to your maximum Hit Points.

[Vambrace of Gorum](/Equipment.aspx?ID=3834)
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Unique" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=161" />
<trait label="Artifact" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=253" />
<trait label="Divine" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=48" />
<trait label="Magical" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=103" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Battlecry!](/Sources.aspx?ID=268) pg. 125

<row gap="medium">

**Usage** held in 1 hand

**Bulk** 2
</row>

<row gap="medium">

 

 

 
</row>

</column>

---

When the [Lord in Iron](/Deities.aspx?ID=283) shattered, immeasurable fragments fell to Golarion as pieces of metal. This piece of his armor has been shaped into the _Vambrace of Gorum_, a _[supreme reinforcing ](/Equipment.aspx?ID=2811) [high-grade adamantine shield](/Equipment.aspx?ID=2812)_ (Hardness 20, HP 160, BT 80). Pieces of sharp iron stick out, acting as _[+3 major striking ](/Equipment.aspx?ID=2861) [shield spikes](/Weapons.aspx?ID=397)_. The _Vambrace_ still holds some of the deity’s power. When the shield is broken, small fragments of metal explode outward, dealing 6d6 piercing damage in a 15-foot [cone](/Rules.aspx?ID=2386) (DC 40 [basic](/Rules.aspx?ID=2297) Reflex save).

**Activate—Blade of Iron** <actions string="Two Actions" /> ([concentrate](/Traits.aspx?ID=561), [divine](/Traits.aspx?ID=579), [manipulate](/Traits.aspx?ID=645)) **Frequency** once per day;   **Effect** The shield reforms into a _+3 high-grade adamantine major striking [greatsword](/Weapons.aspx?ID=379)_ for 1 minute. While wielding this sword, you gain a +1 circumstance bonus to AC for each adjacent enemy (up to a +4 bonus).

**Activate—Blood of Iron** <actions string="Single Action" /> ([aura](/Traits.aspx?ID=542), [divine](/Traits.aspx?ID=579)) **Frequency** once per day;  **Requirements** The _Vambrace of Gorum_ is in its shield form; **Effect** Your shield becomes an empowering symbol of the thrill of battle. You and your allies within 10 feet of you gain 30 [temporary Hit Points](/Rules.aspx?ID=2321) that last for 1 hour, and reduce your [clumsy](/Conditions.aspx?ID=61), [enfeebled](/Conditions.aspx?ID=71), [frightened](/Conditions.aspx?ID=76), and [stupefied](/Conditions.aspx?ID=94) conditions by 1.

**Activate—Bones of Iron** <actions string="Reaction" /> ;  **Frequency** once per 10 minutes; **Trigger** You use the shield to [Shield Block](/Feats.aspx?ID=5212) and the attack overcomes the shield’s Hardness;  **Effect** The iron spikes lash out at the creature who made the attack. The creature takes 6d6 piercing damage and 3d6 [persistent bleed damage](/Conditions.aspx?ID=86) (DC 40 [basic](/Rules.aspx?ID=2297) Reflex save).

**Destruction** If the _Vambrace of Gorum_ is broken, buried under a rose bush in [Nirvana](/Planes.aspx?ID=44), and left undisturbed for 100 years, it loses all its magic and becomes a standard [steel shield](/Shields.aspx?ID=19).

The blade of this _+2 [greater striking](/Equipment.aspx?ID=280) [wounding](/Equipment.aspx?ID=309) [scythe](/Weapons.aspx?ID=39)_ is sharp enough to produce a whistling sound when swung through the air. The shaft is made of ebony wood with a sickly shine to it, much like the shine of infected wounds and contaminated water.

**Activate** <actions string="Reaction" /> command;   **Trigger** An enemy critically succeeds at an attempt to [Disarm](/Actions.aspx?ID=41) you;  **Effect** As the scythe leaves your hand, it drinks the triggering creature's blood. The creature must succeed at a DC 30 Fortitude save or become [drained 2](/Conditions.aspx?ID=10) (drained 3 on a critical failure). If the triggering creature becomes drained, you gain temporary Hit Points equal to the triggering creature's level. You lose any remaining temporary Hit Points after 1 minute.

**Activate** <actions string="Reaction" /> command;  **Frequency** once per hour; **Trigger** You critically succeed at a Strike against a living opponent;  **Effect** The scythe drains life essence from your opponent into you. You gain a number of temporary Hit Points equal to half the slashing damage the scythe dealt to the foe. You lose any remaining temporary Hit Points after 1 minute.

---

This compact compass repurposes ancient technology to draw fantastic powers from the mysterious magical items called [_aeon stones_](/Equipment.aspx?ID=407). It serves as a badge of office for agents of the Pathfinder Society and as a status symbol among adventurers of any stripe. A _wayfinder_ functions as a compass.

 An indentation in the middle of the _wayfinder_ can hold a single _aeon stone_. Placing an _aeon stone_ in this indentation provides you all the benefits of having the _aeon stone_ orbiting your head, but it protects the stone from being noticed or stolen as easily. You invest a _wayfinder_ and the _aeon stone_ within it simultaneously, and they count as only one item toward your investiture limit. An invested _aeon stone_ slotted in a _wayfinder_ also grants its resonant power.

 If you have more than one _wayfinder_ with an invested _aeon stone_ on your person at a given time, destructive interference from their resonance prevents you from gaining benefits from any of them. You can still benefit from additional _aeon stones_ orbiting your head, just not in _wayfinders_.

**Activate** <actions string="Single Action" /> command;     **Effect** The _wayfinder_ is targeted by a 1st-level [_light_](/Spells.aspx?ID=171) spell.

---

An _archaic wayfinder_ functions as a compass and acts as a repository for one cantrip cast into it. To fill an _archaic wayfinder_, a spellcaster casts the chosen cantrip into the empty device, providing any necessary cost; the spell cannot be one that is normally cast as a free action or reaction. Activating an _archaic wayfinder_ is the same as the casting for the relevant spell. Once it has been activated, it becomes empty again. An _archaic wayfinder_ can hold an aeon stone and activate its resonant power. An _archaic wayfinder_ counts against the limit of one _wayfinder_ with a slotted resonant _[aeon stone](/Equipment.aspx?ID=407)_.

A _bi-resonant wayfinder_ is inlaid with intricate platinum wires in a complex array of conduits for magical energy. These conduits control the resonant interference of _aeon stones_. A _bi-resonant wayfinder_ works just like a regular _wayfinder_ except it has two _aeon stone_ slots, and the _aeon stones_ in both slots grant their resonant powers without interfering with each other. The _bi-resonant wayfinder_ and the two _aeon stones_ count as two items toward your investiture limit.

---

A _shining wayfinder_ is a polished silver compass blessed by the power of benevolent deities. It has the usual functions of a _wayfinder_, except instead of an activation to cast _light_, the shining wayfinder has the following two activations.

**Activate** <actions string="Two Actions" /> command, Interact;     **Effect** You hold the _wayfinder_ and ask for guidance. The wayfinder casts [_guidance_](/Spells.aspx?ID=142) on you.

**Activate** <actions string="Two Actions" /> command, Interact;  **Frequency** once per day;   **Effect** You call upon the wayfinder’s divine blessings for yourself and your allies. The wayfinder casts [_bless_](/Spells.aspx?ID=25), with an emanation centered on itself. Once per turn, you can use a single action, which has the [concentrate](/Traits.aspx?ID=32) trait, to increase the emanation’s radius by 5 feet.

A _vanishing wayfinder_ is crafted of ivory chased with gold and silver. It has the usual functions of a _wayfinder_ and the following additional activation.

**Activate** <actions string="Two Actions" /> command, Interact;  **Frequency** once per day;   **Effect** You turn the _wayfinder_ in a circle while invoking its command word, gaining the effects of a 2nd-level [_invisibility_](/Spells.aspx?ID=164) spell for 5 minutes.

---

_Chronicler wayfinders_ bear a mystical connection to the _Pathfinder Chronicles_ themselves, granting them the ability to assist in situations where unusual lore is needed by drawing on lore from a particular topic. Each _chronicler wayfinder_ is attuned to a specific [Lore](/Skills.aspx?ID=8) skill, chosen at the time of creation. In addition to the effects of a _wayfinder_, a chronicler wayfinder has the following activation.

**Activate** <actions string="Single Action" /> envision;     **Effect** You tap into the _Pathfinder Chronicles_ on the _chronicler wayfinder's_ attuned topic, gaining the effects of a [Recall Knowledge](/Actions.aspx?ID=26) action with the chosen Lore skill. For the Lore check's modifier, use whichever is better of +12 or your own modifier, using your level as your proficiency bonus even if you're untrained in the attuned Lore skill.

---

Worn on a chain around the neck, a _Razmiri wayfinder_ functions as a [compass](/Equipment.aspx?ID=16) and provides its wearer a +1 item bonus to [Deception](/Skills.aspx?ID=5) checks to [Lie](/Actions.aspx?ID=47) or [Impersonate](/Actions.aspx?ID=46). _Razmiri wayfinders_ can also be used to grant temporary healing, making it easier for the wearer to impersonate a divine spellcaster.

**Activate** <actions string="Single Action" /> envision;  **Frequency** three times per day;   **Effect** You touch an adjacent creature, granting them 3d8 temporary Hit Points for 1 hour.

**Activate** <actions string="Single Action" /> manipulate;  **Frequency** once per day;   **Effect** You touch an adjacent creature and attempt a [counteract](/Rules.aspx?ID=371) check against one [poison](/Traits.aspx?ID=126) or [disease](/Traits.aspx?ID=46) afflicting the creature. On a success, you halt the effects of the poison or disease for 1 day, rather than removing it. This temporarily relieves any penalties imposed by the affliction but doesn't cure the effect or count against its duration; the poison or disease is merely halted for a time, and it resumes where it left off once this effect ends.

_Fashionable wayfinders_ allow you to be dressed for success in almost any situation. In addition to the effects of a _wayfinder_, a _fashionable wayfinder_ can attune to up to three sets of mundane clothing in your possession during your daily preparations. A _fashionable wayfinder_ has the following activation.

**Activate** <actions string="Single Action" /> envision;     **Effect** You call one of the attuned sets of clothing onto yourself, changing clothes instantly and leaving you either holding the old set of clothing or with the old set folded neatly on the floor if you don't have a free hand to hold it. This activation can't change you into or out of a suit of armor of any kind. While the activation can transport the chosen attuned set of clothing onto you from up to 60 feet away, it can't transport any other creatures or items that might have been stored in the clothing.

level="2"
right="Item 13"
pfs="Standard"
>
Homeward Wayfinder
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Uncommon" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=159" />
<trait label="Conjuration" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=33" />
<trait label="Evocation" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=65" />
<trait label="Invested" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=98" />
<trait label="Magical" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=103" />
<trait label="Teleportation" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=156" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [PFS Guide](/Sources.aspx?ID=50) pg. 122

_[**PFS Note**](/pathfinder-society) All characters affiliated with the Pathfinder Society have access to this item_

**Price** 2,750 gp

<row gap="medium">

**Usage** worn

</row>

**Access** Member of the Pathfinder Society.

</column>

---

_Homeward wayfinders_ are powerful escape tools in the hands of a Pathfinder agent, drawing upon a special connection to the Maze of the Open Road. In addition to the effects of a _wayfinder_, a _homeward wayfinder_ attunes itself to the most recent Pathfinder Lodge you've visited and has the following activation.

**Activate** <actions string="" /> 10 minutes (command, Interact);  **Frequency** once per day;   **Effect** You teleport back to the attuned Pathfinder Lodge, as long as you are no more than 100 miles away. This [teleportation](/Traits.aspx?ID=156) effect fails if you would bring another creature with you, even if you're carrying it in an [extradimensional](/Traits.aspx?ID=67) space.

Hummingbird Wayfinder
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Uncommon" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=159" />

_Hummingbird wayfinders_ blend a few Arcadian secrets into the original _wayfinder_ design, allowing the _wayfinder_ to gain mobility for a time and act as a spy. In addition to the effects of a _wayfinder_, a _hummingbird wayfinder_ has the following activation.

**Activate** <actions string="Two Actions" /> command, Interact;  **Frequency** once per hour;   **Effect** You cause the _wayfinder_ to transform into a Tiny bee hummingbird, only 2 inches long. Other than the _wayfinder_ being a visible bird, this has the effects of [_prying eye_](/Spells.aspx?ID=239). In addition to [Seeking](/Actions.aspx?ID=84) through the hummingbird, you can activate any [_aeon stone_](/Equipment.aspx?ID=407) within the _wayfinder_ as if the _wayfinder_ were still on your person. When the effect ends, the _wayfinder_ transforms back to normal in its current position. Damaging the bird ends the effect but does not destroy the _wayfinder_.

Item 2 Wayfinder Uncommon Evocation Invested Magical Source Core Rulebook pg. 617 PFS Note All Pathfinders have access. Price 28 gp Usage worn This compact compass repurposes ancient technology to draw fantastic powers from the mysterious magical items called aeon stones . It serves as a badge of office for agents of the Pathfinder Society and as a status symbol among adventurers of any stripe. A wayfinder functions as a compass. An indentation in the middle of the wayfinder can hold a single aeon stone . Placing an aeon stone in this indentation provides you all the benefits of having the aeon stone orbiting your head, but it protects the stone from being noticed or stolen as easily. You invest a wayfinder and the aeon stone within it simultaneously, and they count as only one item toward your investiture limit. An invested aeon stone slotted in a wayfinder also grants its resonant power. If you have more than one wayfinder with an invested aeon stone on your person at a given time, destructive interference from their resonance prevents you from gaining benefits from any of them. You can still benefit from additional aeon stones orbiting your head, just not in wayfinders . Activate Single Action command; Effect The wayfinder is targeted by a 1st-level light spell. Item 2 Archaic Wayfinder Uncommon Evocation Invested Magical Source World Guide pg. 17 PFS Note All characters have access to the archaic wayfinder Price 30 gp Usage held in 1 hand Activate Cast a Spell An archaic wayfinder functions as a compass and acts as a repository for one cantrip cast into it. To fill an archaic wayfinder , a spellcaster casts the chosen cantrip into the empty device, providing any necessary cost; the spell cannot be one that is normally cast as a free action or reaction. Activating an archaic wayfinder is the same as the casting for the relevant spell. Once it has been activated, it becomes empty again. An archaic wayfinder can hold an aeon stone and activate its resonant power. An archaic wayfinder counts against the limit of one wayfinder with a slotted resonant aeon stone . Item 4 Wayfinder of Rescue Uncommon Evocation Invested Magical Source PFS Scenario #1-03: Escaping the Grave pg. 42 Price 80 gp Usage worn As a standard wayfinder , but once per day you can activate it to cast heal on a creature other than yourself, using either the one-action or two-action version of heal as a 1st-level spell. Item 6 Bi-Resonant Wayfinder Uncommon Evocation Illusion Invested Magical Source Character Guide pg. 110 Price 200 gp Usage worn Access A character who is a member of the Pathfinder Society has access to this option. A bi-resonant wayfinder is inlaid with intricate platinum wires in a complex array of conduits for magical energy. These conduits control the resonant interference of aeon stones . A bi-resonant wayfinder works just like a regular wayfinder except it has two aeon stone slots, and the aeon stones in both slots grant their resonant powers without interfering with each other. The bi-resonant wayfinder and the two aeon stones count as two items toward your investiture limit. Item 4 Shining Wayfinder Uncommon Abjuration Divination Evocation Invested Magical Source Character Guide pg. 111 Price 100 gp Usage worn Access A character who is a member of the Pathfinder Society has access to this option. A shining wayfinder is a polished silver compass blessed by the power of benevolent deities. It has the usual functions of a wayfinder , except instead of an activation to cast light , the shining wayfinder has the following two activations. Activate Two Actions command, Interact; Effect You hold the wayfinder and ask for guidance. The wayfinder casts guidance on you. Activate Two Actions command, Interact; Frequency once per day; Effect You call upon the wayfinder’s divine blessings for yourself and your allies. The wayfinder casts bless , with an emanation centered on itself. Once per turn, you can use a single action, which has the concentrate trait, to increase the emanation’s radius by 5 feet. Item 5 Vanishing Wayfinder Uncommon Evocation Illusion Invested Magical Source Character Guide pg. 112 Price 150 gp Usage worn Access A character who is a member of the Pathfinder Society has access to this option. A vanishing wayfinder is crafted of ivory chased with gold and silver. It has the usual functions of a wayfinder and the following additional activation. Activate Two Actions command, Interact; Frequency once per day; Effect You turn the wayfinder in a circle while invoking its command word, gaining the effects of a 2nd-level invisibility spell for 5 minutes. Item 6 Chronicler Wayfinder Uncommon Evocation Invested Magical Source PFS Guide pg. 30 PFS Note Players can gain access to faction-specific gear by taking the corresponding Faction Gear Access Game Reward, available when they reach 20 reputation with the respective faction. Price 200 gp Usage worn Access Member of the Pathfinder Society. Chronicler wayfinders bear a mystical connection to the Pathfinder Chronicles themselves, granting them the ability to assist in situations where unusual lore is needed by drawing on lore from a particular topic. Each chronicler wayfinder is attuned to a specific Lore skill, chosen at the time of creation. In addition to the effects of a wayfinder , a chronicler wayfinder has the following activation. Activate Single Action envision; Effect You tap into the Pathfinder Chronicles on the chronicler wayfinder's attuned topic, gaining the effects of a Recall Knowledge action with the chosen Lore skill. For the Lore check's modifier, use whichever is better of +12 or your own modifier, using your level as your proficiency bonus even if you're untrained in the attuned Lore skill. Item 10 Razmiri Wayfinder Uncommon Illusion Magical Necromancy Source PFS Guide pg. 72 Price 900 gp Usage worn Worn on a chain around the neck, a Razmiri wayfinder functions as a compass and provides its wearer a +1 item bonus to Deception checks to Lie or Impersonate. Razmiri wayfinders can also be used to grant temporary healing, making it easier for the wearer to impersonate a divine spellcaster. Activate Single Action envision; Frequency three times per day; Effect You touch an adjacent creature, granting them 3d8 temporary Hit Points for 1 hour. Activate Single Action manipulate; Frequency once per day; Effect You touch an adjacent creature and attempt a counteract check against one poison or disease afflicting the creature. On a success, you halt the effects of the poison or disease for 1 day, rather than removing it. This temporarily relieves any penalties imposed by the affliction but doesn't cure the effect or count against its duration; the poison or disease is merely halted for a time, and it resumes where it left off once this effect ends. Item 9 Elemental Wayfinder (Air) Uncommon Air Evocation Invested Magical Source PFS Guide pg. 122 PFS Note All characters affiliated with the Pathfinder Society have access to this item Price 650 gp Usage worn Access Member of the Pathfinder Society. Pathfinder Society researchers recently created elemental wayfinders with the assistance of the Society's elemental allies. In addition to the effects of a wayfinder , these wayfinders each grant the ability to cast a particular elemental spell once per day, and can assist Pathfinders in exploring areas associated with their element. Additionally, you can cast feather fall as a primal innate spell once every 10 minutes. Activate Two Actions command; Frequency once per day; Effect The wayfinder casts a 4th-level lightning bolt . Item 3 Fashionable Wayfinder Uncommon Conjuration Invested Magical Source PFS Guide pg. 122 PFS Note All characters affiliated with the Pathfinder Society have access to this item Price 50 gp Usage worn Access Member of the Pathfinder Society. Fashionable wayfinders allow you to be dressed for success in almost any situation. In addition to the effects of a wayfinder , a fashionable wayfinder can attune to up to three sets of mundane clothing in your possession during your daily preparations. A fashionable wayfinder has the following activation. Activate Single Action envision; Effect You call one of the attuned sets of clothing onto yourself, changing clothes instantly and leaving you either holding the old set of clothing or with the old set folded neatly on the floor if you don't have a free hand to hold it. This activation can't change you into or out of a suit of armor of any kind. Item 12 Hummingbird Wayfinder Uncommon Evocation Invested Magical Transmutation Source PFS Guide pg. 122 PFS Note All characters affiliated with the Pathfinder Society have access to this item Price 1,750 gp Usage worn Access Member of the Pathfinder Society. >
[Vapor Sphere](/Equipment.aspx?ID=1036)
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Consumable" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=36" />
<trait label="Magical" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=103" />
<trait label="Talisman" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=155" />
<trait label="Transmutation" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=157" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Secrets of Magic](/Sources.aspx?ID=96) pg. 176

**Price** 900 gp

<row gap="medium">

**Usage** affixed to armor

</row>

<row gap="medium">
<row gap="tiny"><row>**Activate**</row><actions string="Reaction" /><row>envision</row></row>

 

**Trigger** You trigger a trap's reaction or an enemy that was [undetected](/Conditions.aspx?ID=39) by you makes an attack against you

**Requirement** You're an expert in the affixed armor and an expert in Reflex saves.
</row>

</column>

---

Within this strange glass sphere swirls a cloud of smoke that occasionally appears as if it's trying to escape. You react to a surprise encounter with haste, activating this talisman and causing your body to momentarily become like vapor. Against the trap's reaction or the attack, you gain resistance 25 to physical damage and are immune to precision damage. This effect also prevents the reaction or attack from physically moving you (such as falling down a pit or being knocked [prone](/Conditions.aspx?ID=31)), and after the reaction or attack, you can [Fly](/Actions.aspx?ID=94) 5 feet. When you end this flight, you leave your vaporous state and are exposed to any danger still at your location.

</column>

>
[Vaporous Pipe](/Equipment.aspx?ID=2198)
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Magical" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=103" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Treasure Vault (Remastered)](/Sources.aspx?ID=191) pg. 116

**Price** 340 gp

<row gap="medium">

**Usage** held in 1 hand

</row>

<row gap="medium">

 

 

 
</row>

</column>

---

This hand-polished pipe is carved from oak and releases small wisps of smoke even when unlit. As long as you're holding a _vaporous pipe_, you don't take a circumstance penalty to Perception checks due to thick smoke, and you can't [suffocate](/Rules.aspx?ID=468) from smoke and heated air (such as within a [wildfire](/Rules.aspx?ID=664)). As long as you are holding the pipe, you also gain resistance to fire equal to half your level.

**Activate** <actions string="Single Action" /> ([manipulate](/Traits.aspx?ID=645)) **Frequency** once per hour;   **Effect** You draw on the pipe and then blow a massive cloud of smoke that fills a 30-foot emanation that includes your space. All creatures within the smoke cloud are [concealed](/Conditions.aspx?ID=4) from each other and from creatures outside the smoke, though you can still see clearly within it. The smoke dissipates after 3 rounds, or after 1 round if subjected to a strong wind.

fields.text: Item 7 Vaporous Pipe Conjuration Magical Source Treasure Vault pg. 116 Price 340 gp Usage held in 1 hand This hand-polished pipe is carved from oak and releases small wisps of smoke even when unlit. As long as you’re holding a vaporous pipe , you don’t take a circumstance penalty to Perception checks due to thick smoke, and you can’t suffocate from smoke and heated air (such as within a wildfire). As long as you are holding the pipe, you also gain resistance to fire equal to half your level. Activate Single Action Interact; Frequency once per hour; Effect You draw on the pipe and then blow a massive cloud of smoke that fills a 30-foot emanation that includes your space. All creatures within the smoke cloud are concealed from each other and from creatures outside the smoke, though you can still see clearly within it. The smoke dissipates after 3 rounds, or after 1 round if subjected to a strong wind.

These tattoos are created using designs and techniques from Varisian culture. Such tattoos often depict the Varisian rune for one of the seven schools of magic, but one might instead show a creature or celestial phenomenon associated with the school, depicted in traditional Varisian iconography. The tattoo allows you to understand and speak Varisian. If you already know that language, you instead gain a +1 item bonus on [Diplomacy](/Skills.aspx?ID=39) checks you make when speaking [Varisian](/Languages.aspx?ID=174) to someone who understands it.

Each description lists the school of each Varisian emblem, and the tattoo has the trait of that school. The spell the tattoo can cast is from its school. As with the Thassilonian magic that was once so prevalent in Varisia, these tattoos lack a symbol of [divination](/Traits.aspx?ID=47).

**Activate** <actions string="" /> The actions required to Activate the tattoo are the same as those needed to cast its spell;  **Frequency** once per day;   **Effect** The tattoo casts its spell.

These tattoos are created using designs and techniques from Varisian culture. Such tattoos often depict the Varisian rune for one of the seven schools of magic, but one might instead show a creature or celestial phenomenon associated with the school, depicted in traditional Varisian iconography. The tattoo allows you to understand and speak Varisian. If you already know that language, you instead gain a +1 item bonus on [Diplomacy](/Skills.aspx?ID=39) checks you make when speaking [Varisian](/Languages.aspx?ID=174) to someone who understands it.

Each description lists the school of each Varisian emblem, and the tattoo has the trait of that school. The spell the tattoo can cast is from its school. As with the Thassilonian magic that was once so prevalent in Varisia, these tattoos lack a symbol of [divination](/Traits.aspx?ID=47).

**Activate** <actions string="" /> The actions required to Activate the tattoo are the same as those needed to cast its spell;  **Frequency** once per day;   **Effect** The tattoo casts its spell.

---

These tattoos are created using designs and techniques from Varisian culture. Such tattoos often depict the Varisian rune for one of the seven schools of magic, but one might instead show a creature or celestial phenomenon associated with the school, depicted in traditional Varisian iconography. The tattoo allows you to understand and speak Varisian. If you already know that language, you instead gain a +1 item bonus on [Diplomacy](/Skills.aspx?ID=39) checks you make when speaking [Varisian](/Languages.aspx?ID=174) to someone who understands it.

Each description lists the school of each Varisian emblem, and the tattoo has the trait of that school. The spell the tattoo can cast is from its school. As with the Thassilonian magic that was once so prevalent in Varisia, these tattoos lack a symbol of [divination](/Traits.aspx?ID=47).

**Activate** <actions string="" /> The actions required to Activate the tattoo are the same as those needed to cast its spell;  **Frequency** once per day;   **Effect** The tattoo casts its spell.

>
[Vashu's Ninth Life](/Equipment.aspx?ID=3150)
</title>

<spoilers>May contain spoilers from Season of Ghosts</spoilers>

<traits>
<trait label="Unique" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=161" />
<trait label="Magical" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=103" />
<trait label="Transmutation" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=157" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Pathfinder #198: No Breath to Cry](/Sources.aspx?ID=224) pg. 77

**Price** 700 gp

<row gap="medium">

**Usage** held in 1 hand

**Bulk** 1
</row>

<row gap="medium">
**Base Weapon** [Katana](/Weapons.aspx?ID=411)
</row>

<row gap="medium">

 

 

 
</row>

</column>

---

This _+1 striking [ghost touch](/Equipment.aspx?ID=2840) [katana](/Weapons.aspx?ID=411)_ is made from a whisker stolen from the king of cats over three hundred years ago by a catfolk rogue named Vashu Vigaru. He sought the magic of the whisker to preternaturally extend his life, and some believe he still lives, having successfully divested himself of the sword to escape the king's wrath in the end.

**Activate** <actions string="Free Action" /> (envision);  **Frequency** once per hour; **Trigger** Your turn ends;  **Effect** You extend your senses through the blade, allowing you to react to nearby movement. _Vashu's Ninth Life_	 gains the [parry](/Traits.aspx?ID=667) trait and raises itself into parrying position, granting you a +1 circumstance bonus to AC until the start of your next turn.

**Activate** <actions string="Reaction" /> (envision);  **Frequency** once per day;   **Effect** A portion of the slain creature's life force travels through the blade and into your soul, bolstering your own life. You gain the benefits of the [Diehard](/Feats.aspx?ID=5140) feat for 1 minute. This causes you to die from the dying condition at dying 5 rather than dying 4.

<column gap="tiny">

</column>

>
[Vat-Grown Brain](/Equipment.aspx?ID=2419)
</title>

<spoilers>May contain spoilers from Gatewalkers</spoilers>

<traits>
<trait label="Rare" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=137" />
<trait label="Alchemical" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=6" />
<trait label="Consumable" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=36" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Pathfinder #189: Dreamers of the Nameless Spires](/Sources.aspx?ID=195) pg. 75

**Price** 190 gp

<row gap="medium">

**Usage** held in 2 hands

**Bulk** 1
</row>

<row gap="medium">
<row gap="tiny"><row>**Activate**</row><actions string="Three Actions" /><row>Interact</row></row>

 

 

 
</row>

</column>

---

A malformed, artificial brain pulses with alchemical life inside a nutrient-rich vat. When the vat-grown brain is activated, it attempts to [counteract](/Rules.aspx?ID=371) one condition of your choice that was gained from an ability with the [mental](/Traits.aspx?ID=106) trait, which it does by drawing the negative mental impressions into itself. However, the artificial brain is not robust, and the strain of the transfer quickly destroys it. The vat-grown brain has a counteract level of 5 and a +17 modifier on the roll.

A _vaultbreaker's harness_ has four pockets across the chest. The pockets contain a set of [infiltrator's thieves' tools](/Equipment.aspx?ID=58), infiltrator picks, a [levered crowbar](/Equipment.aspx?ID=18), and a [glass cutter](/Equipment.aspx?ID=870). These items are magically bound to the harness; if they are more than 1 foot away from you, they disappear, then reappear in the harness at the next sunset. [Broken](/Conditions.aspx?ID=2) or destroyed items similarly reappear, restored, in their proper pockets at sunset.

**Activate** <actions string="Single Action" /> ([manipulate](/Traits.aspx?ID=645))    **Effect** You cinch the harness to prepare for mischief. You gain a +1 item bonus to [Stealth](/Skills.aspx?ID=15) checks and a +10-foot item bonus to your Speed for 1 minute.

<title
    level="1"
    right="Item 7+"
    pfs="Standard"
>
[Veiled Figurehead](/Equipment.aspx?ID=2635)
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Figurehead" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=512" />
<trait label="Magical" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=103" />
<trait label="Water" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=165" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Rage of Elements](/Sources.aspx?ID=205) pg. 179

<row gap="medium">

**Usage** attached to a ship's bow

</row>

<row gap="medium">

 

 

 
</row>

</column>

---

This figurehead is carved in the shape of a [humanoid](/Traits.aspx?ID=91), but it has no facial features whatsoever.

**Activate—Veil!** <actions string="" /> 1 minute ([concentrate](/Traits.aspx?ID=32), [illusion](/Traits.aspx?ID=92), [visual](/Traits.aspx?ID=163)) **Frequency** once per day;   **Effect** You change the appearance of the ship in minor but noticeable ways. Its general size and shape can't be changed, but you can alter surface details to your liking. Flags and sails can be recolored and given new markings, and the overall material of the ship can appear a different color or quality. Wear and surface damage (like small holes, tears, and burns) can be masked to make the vessel look unblemished, or you can create such damage and wear. The figurehead itself shifts to fit the change and gains a face to match the rest of the ship. The illusion lasts for 6 hours or until you Dismiss this effect.

 Any creature that boards the ship or uses the [Seek](/Actions.aspx?ID=84) action to examine it disbelieves the illusion if it succeeds at a DC 25 Perception check.

<column gap="tiny">

</column>

<title
level="2"
right="Item 7"
pfs="Standard"
>
Veiled Figurehead
</title>

<traits>

</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Rage of Elements](/Sources.aspx?ID=205) pg. 179

**Price** 335 gp

<row gap="medium">

</row>

</column>

<title
level="2"
right="Item 14"
pfs="Standard"
>
Veiled Figurehead (Greater)
</title>

<traits>

</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Rage of Elements](/Sources.aspx?ID=205) pg. 179

**Price** 4,000 gp

<row gap="medium">

</row>

</column>

---

The DC to disbelieve is 33, and the illusion lasts up to 24 hours. Activating a _greater veiled figurehead_ also extends the illusion to those on the ship. The figurehead casts a [_veil_](/Spells.aspx?ID=355) spell upon them, except it targets everyone on board when activated, and it alters their clothing to a general look that matches the new appearance of the ship. In addition, it can make everyone appear as a specific ancestry, but you must choose the same one for all targets. This effect ends for any target who leaves the ship and ends for all targets if the illusion on the ship ends. A creature that disbelieves the illusion for the ship or any disguised crew member disbelieves the entire illusion.

<title
    level="1"
    right="Item 7"
    pfs=""
>
[Velicarn's Cursed Coin](/Equipment.aspx?ID=5204)
</title>

<spoilers>May contain spoilers from Bastion of Blasphemies</spoilers>

<traits>
<trait label="Unique" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=723" />
<trait label="Cursed" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=567" />
<trait label="Invested" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=637" />
<trait label="Occult" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=662" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Pathfinder #224: Bastion of Blasphemies](/Sources.aspx?ID=357) pg. 241

<row gap="medium">

**Usage** held in 1 hand

**Bulk** L
</row>

<row gap="medium">

 

 

 
</row>

</column>

---

This platinum coin was minted in Caliphas in the year 4192, the same year that Velicarn, the eponymous bastard of Bastardhall, was born. While the design of coins has changed in the 500 or so years since this one was minted, anyone who is at least an expert in [Society](/Skills.aspx?ID=47) recognizes that this coin’s design resembles no known Ustalavic tradition—and in fact, when the coin became cursed on that vile night in 4213, its imagery forever changed. In the present day, one side of the coin depicts a distorted image of the Arudora family crest, while the other depicts a set of monstrous eyes peering through the cracks in a crumbling wall (identifiable as the religious symbol of Charg with a DC 25 [Religion](/Skills.aspx?ID=46) check to Recall Knowledge). The coin feels unusually heavy for being made of platinum, and no merchant will accept it as cash as a result. Most merchants and collectors who are presented with the coin have an instinctual distaste for its strange weight and slightly greasy feel. As soon as someone carries _Velicarn’s cursed coin_ for longer than a minute, it automatically becomes invested, fuses with that person, and continues to count against that character’s invested items, even without being reinvested each day. As long as the coin is carried, sahkils prefer to target the coin’s carrier with their attacks (although they are not forced to do so), often behaving as if they can smell the “stink of the Typhon Wheel” on them. Fortunately for a character cursed by this item, the coin has no further debilitating effects, save for when it is activated.

_Vengeful demon's tears_ is an infamously noxious spirit mixed into a potent magical cocktail and traditionally packaged in a gourd adorned with an engraving of a terrifying demonic face. Drinking it feels akin to lighting your throat on fire and putting it out with an herbal tonic. When you activate this potion, you gain the [quickened](/Conditions.aspx?ID=89) condition for 3 rounds and can use the extra action each round to Strike, Stride, or to take the following action.

</title>

<spoilers>May contain spoilers from Triumph of the Tusk</spoilers>

<traits>
<trait label="Uncommon" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=159" />
<trait label="Magical" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=103" />
<trait label="Poison" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=126" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Pathfinder #208: Hoof, Cinder, and Storm](/Sources.aspx?ID=250) pg. 79

**Price** 350 gp

<row gap="medium">

**Usage** held in 1 hand

**Bulk** 1
</row>

<row gap="medium">
**Base Weapon** [Flail](/Weapons.aspx?ID=374)
</row>

<row gap="medium">

 

 

 
</row>

</column>

---

With careful alchemical treatments, orc weaponsmiths can enhance the durability and flexibility of giant scorpion tails to create multi-headed _[+1 striking](/Equipment.aspx?ID=2861) [flails](/Weapons.aspx?ID=374)_. Additional enchantments allow the stingers to generate their own venom. When you would apply this flail’s [critical specialization](/WeaponGroups.aspx?ID=7), you can instead deal 1d6 [persistent poison damage](/Conditions.aspx?ID=86) to the target. You gain an item bonus to the persistent poison damage equal to the weapon’s item bonus to attack rolls.

**Activate—Envenom** <actions string="Single Action" /> ([manipulate](/Traits.aspx?ID=645), [poison](/Traits.aspx?ID=669)) **Frequency** once per day;   **Effect** You temporarily fill the flail’s stingers with venom. The next successful Strike you make with it before the end of your next turn deals 2d6 persistent poison damage to the target. If the Strike critically succeeds and if you would apply persistent poison damage with this weapon’s alternate critical specialization, you combine the two effects to deal 3d6 persistent poison damage to the target.

<column gap="tiny">

</column>

This large wooden [buckler](/Shields.aspx?ID=17) (Hardness 6, HP 24, BT 12) is alive with creeping vines and mossy growths that shift in the air almost imperceptibly. 

**Activate—Grasping Vines** <actions string="Free Action" /> ([concentrate](/Traits.aspx?ID=561), plant) **Frequency** once per day; **Trigger** You use the _verdant buckler_ to Shield Block a melee Strike; **Requirements** ; **Effect** The attacking creature must succeed at a DC 24 Reflex save or be [grabbed](/Conditions.aspx?ID=77) by the shield’s animated vines ([restrained](/Conditions.aspx?ID=90) on a critical failure). The affected creature is grappled or restrained for 1 round, until it [Escapes](/Actions.aspx?ID=2296) (DC 24), or you move, whichever comes first.

This poultice of herbs and dried berries found throughout Isger was invented by those fighting against Cheliax's diabolic intrusion and those warring against demons at the Worldwound. **Source** [PFS Guide](/Sources.aspx?ID=50) pg. 100 **Usage** held in 2 hands **Bulk** L **Activate**Interact --- This specialized cream serves as a repellent to stave off insects. The repellent also binds with a number of common insect venoms, dulling the potency and giving the wearer's immune system a boost to resist venoms. Once applied to your skin, the repellent grants you an item bonus to Fortitude saving throws against [poisons](/Traits.aspx?ID=126) for 4 hours. In addition, any arthropods (insects, spiders, scorpions, crabs, and similar invertebrate animals) must attempt a Will save when attempting to attack you with a melee Strike, or with a [swarm](/Traits.aspx?ID=239) attack such as the [spider swarm's](/Monsters.aspx?ID=385) swarming bites. The arthropod then becomes temporarily immune for 1 minute. **Critical Success** The creature can act normally.
**Success** The creature is [frightened 1](/Conditions.aspx?ID=19).
**Failure** The creature is frightened 2.
**Critical Failure** The creature is frightened 2 and [fleeing](/Conditions.aspx?ID=17). Vermin Repellent Agent (Lesser) **Source** [PFS Guide](/Sources.aspx?ID=50) pg. 100 **Price** 8 gp **Bulk** L --- You gain a +1 item bonus and the save DC is 17. Vermin Repellent Agent (Moderate) **Source** [PFS Guide](/Sources.aspx?ID=50) pg. 100 **Price** 75 gp **Bulk** L --- You gain a +2 item bonus and the save DC is 24. Vermin Repellent Agent (Greater) **Source** [PFS Guide](/Sources.aspx?ID=50) pg. 100 **Price** 315 gp **Bulk** L --- You gain a +3 item bonus and the save DC is 29. Vermin Repellent Agent (Major) **Source** [PFS Guide](/Sources.aspx?ID=50) pg. 100 **Price** 1,350 gp **Bulk** L --- You gain a +4 item bonus and the save DC is 35.

    level="1"
    right="Item 15"
    pfs="Limited"
>
[Vernai Shell](/Equipment.aspx?ID=3484)
</title>

<spoilers>May contain spoilers from Prey for Death</spoilers>

<traits>
<trait label="Uncommon" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=721" />
<trait label="Extradimensional" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=596" />
<trait label="Invested" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=637" />
<trait label="Magical" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=644" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Prey for Death](/Sources.aspx?ID=231) pg. 101

**Price** 8,000 gp

<row gap="medium">

**Usage** worn armor

**Bulk** 1
</row>

<row gap="medium">
**Base Armor** [Mantis Shell](/Armor.aspx?ID=30)
</row>

<row gap="medium">

 

 

 
</row>

</column>

---

Made from the finest plates of monstrous insect chitin, this _+2 greater resilient [mantis shell](/Armor.aspx?ID=30)_ offers superior protection from Mediogalti's hot weather while also allowing the wearer to blend into almost any situation and strike with hidden blades. While wearing this armor, you are protected from extreme heat and severe heat effects. Vernai shell armor includes two extradimensional spaces built into each of the armor's gloves, granting the wearer two places to store items. Each glove can hold one item of 1 Bulk or less. While an item is stored in one of the two gloves, there is nothing to indicate that an item is being held inside it. 

**Activate—Store Item** <actions string="Single Action" /> ([manipulate](/Traits.aspx?ID=104))   **Requirements** At least one of the _Vernai shell's_ two extradimensional spaces is empty; **Effect** One item you’re holding with a Bulk of 1 or less vanishes into one of the armor’s extradimensional spaces. 

**Activate—Retrieve Item** <actions string="Free Action" /> ([concentrate](/Traits.aspx?ID=32), [manipulate](/Traits.aspx?ID=104))   **Requirements** An item is stored in at least one of the _Vernai shell's_ extradimensional spaces, and you have a free hand.; **Effect** One item of your choice in either extradimensional space appears in your hand. You can’t Retrieve Item again for 1 minute

<column gap="tiny">

</column>

<title
    level="1"
    right="Item 1"
    pfs="Standard"
>
[Versatile Tinderbox](/Equipment.aspx?ID=2651)
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Magical" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=103" />
<trait label="Wood" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=508" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Rage of Elements](/Sources.aspx?ID=205) pg. 203

**Price** 20 gp

<row gap="medium">

**Usage** held in 1 hand

</row>

<row gap="medium">

 

 

 
</row>

</column>

---

A fine case carved from elegant wood, this tinderbox holds twigs and strips of wood in a selection of six colors. In a typical _versatile tinderbox_, these colors are black, blue, green, magenta, yellow, and violet. When used in lighting a fire, colored tinder alters the flames' color and smoke to match. The box is perfectly carved and constructed to hold tinder, keeping it completely dry, but is incapable of closing if used to hold anything else. The tinderbox replenishes itself; it's never out of tinder when its owner is in need, but it never produces a surplus of tinder either.

</column>

<title
    level="1"
    right="Item 3"
    pfs="Standard"
>
[Vestige Lenses](/Equipment.aspx?ID=767)
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Rare" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=137" />
<trait label="Alchemical" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=6" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Legends](/Sources.aspx?ID=40) pg. 25

**Price** 40 gp

<row gap="medium">

**Usage** worn eyepiece

**Bulk** L
</row>

<row gap="medium">

 

 

 
</row>

</column>

---

These simple lenses are alchemically treated to detect the faint smoke trail from a piece of specially formulated sandalwood incense. This incense has an odor undetectable by most people and a long burn time, making it perfect for discreetly tracking individuals. A stick of this incense costs 1 sp and can safely burn for up to 8 hours. While wearing the lenses, you see alchemical fumes in a distinct green tint, granting you a +1 item bonus to [Survival](/Skills.aspx?ID=16) checks to [Track](/Actions.aspx?ID=66) a creature marked with the incense and to Perception checks to [Seek](/Actions.aspx?ID=84) any alchemical vapors. If the smoke is fresh, Tracking via the incense's fumes might use a lower DC than normal for tracking a creature walking on firm surfaces.

<column gap="tiny">

</column>

<title
    level="1"
    right="Item 20"
    pfs="Standard"
>
[Vial of the Immortal Wellspring](/Equipment.aspx?ID=1655)
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Rare" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=137" />
<trait label="Contract" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=329" />
<trait label="Invested" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=98" />
<trait label="Magical" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=103" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Dark Archive](/Sources.aspx?ID=129) pg. 165

<row gap="medium">

</row>

<row gap="medium">

 

 

 
</row>

</column>

---

At a wellspring, you gave your blood to a force of nature and received a vial from the wellspring's heart in return. Once per 10 minutes, when your [dying](/Conditions.aspx?ID=11) value would increase above 3, you instead become [unconscious](/Conditions.aspx?ID=38) and are no longer dying; this doesn't prevent you from being killed by [death](/Domains.aspx?ID=7) effects or the [doomed](/Conditions.aspx?ID=9) condition. Once per day, from any distance, the entity that holds your _bargained contract_ can possess you and control your actions, leaving you unaware of what goes on. This possession automatically succeeds, regardless of any countermeasures you might take. Normally this lasts for only 1 round if during an encounter, or no longer than a few minutes during exploration. However, the more you rely on the power of the wellspring's heart to survive death, the longer it can possess you the next time it chooses to do so, doubling the amount of time with each use, to a maximum duration of 1 day. Once the entity possesses you, this duration resets.

**Activate** <actions string="Two Actions" /> command;  **Frequency** once per day;   **Effect** You drink from the vial of water that seals your _bargained contract_. You gain the effects of a 9th-level, 2-action [_heal_](/Spells.aspx?ID=148) spell.

<column gap="tiny">

</column>

fields.markdown:
**Source** [Advanced Player's Guide](/Sources.aspx?ID=39) pg. 264 **Usage** worn armor **Bulk** 4 **Base Armor** [Full Plate](/Armor.aspx?ID=13) --- The metal plates of this _+1 [resilient](/Equipment.aspx?ID=279) [full plate](/Armor.aspx?ID=13)_ are covered by a bright tabard featuring a distinctive coat of arms divided into four fields. This insignia magically records your recent victories, displaying one triumph in each field of the coat of arms, allowing you to call upon those victories for aid in future battles. **Activate** envision; **Trigger** You kill or destroy a creature of a level equal to or greater than your _victory plate_ (adjusted as usual if you add fundamental runes to _victory plate_). This creature must have one of the traits listed in the second activation; **Effect** You direct the armor to commemorate your victory. The coat of arms on the armor's tabard shifts to incorporate heraldry related to the slain creature, and the victory is recorded within the tabard. If you have already recorded four victories, choose one to replace with the new victory. **Activate** envision, Interact; **Frequency** once per hour; **Effect** You touch one of the tabard's four fields representing one of your victories and recall your triumph over that creature. That creature vanishes from the tabard, and for 1 minute, you gain resistance 5 to a damage type based on the creature's trait (you gain resistance to only one type, even if the creature has more than one trait that could apply):
  • [Aberration](/Traits.aspx?ID=1) or [Fey](/Traits.aspx?ID=69) mental
  • [Celestial](/Traits.aspx?ID=23) good
  • [Construct](/Traits.aspx?ID=35) poison
  • [Dragon](/Traits.aspx?ID=50) or [Elemental](/Traits.aspx?ID=57) one energy type that matches one of the dragon's or elemental's traits
  • [Fiend](/Traits.aspx?ID=70) evil
  • [Ooze](/Traits.aspx?ID=122) precision, and the resistance is 10
  • [Undead](/Traits.aspx?ID=160) negative
Victory Plate **Source** [Advanced Player's Guide](/Sources.aspx?ID=39) pg. 264 **Price** 675 gp **Bulk** 4 Victory Plate (Greater) **Source** [Advanced Player's Guide](/Sources.aspx?ID=39) pg. 264 **Price** 5,500 gp **Bulk** 4 --- The armor is a _+2 greater resilient full plate_. You can use the second activation once per minute instead of once per hour, and the resistance it grants is 10, or 20 for the ooze's resistance against precision damage.

**Source** [Treasure Vault (Remastered)](/Sources.aspx?ID=191) pg. 129 **Usage** affixed to armor or a weapon --- Carved in this wooden disc is a humanoid eye, painted in muted shades that blend in with the wood. The eye’s pupil continually twitches and moves, scanning its bearer’s surroundings.
  • **Armor** ([revelation](/Traits.aspx?ID=686)) You aren’t [off-guard](/Conditions.aspx?ID=58) to [hidden](/Conditions.aspx?ID=79) or [undetected](/Conditions.aspx?ID=96) creatures of the eye’s level or lower, or creatures of the eye’s level or lower using surprise attack, though you can still be [flanked](/Rules.aspx?ID=2375).
  • **Weapon** When you make a [Strike](/Actions.aspx?ID=2306) with the weapon against a target that’s [concealed](/Conditions.aspx?ID=62), hidden, or undetected, the DC of your flat check to target it is 4 if the target is concealed or 10 if it’s hidden or undetected.
**Activate** Cast a Spell; **Effect** You cast [_detect magic_](/Spells.aspx?ID=66).
