May contain spoilers from Bastion of Blasphemies **Source** [Pathfinder #224: Bastion of Blasphemies](/Sources.aspx?ID=357) pg. 236 **Usage** held in 1 hand **Bulk** L --- When dislodged, mortal fragments like a chewed fingernail, a careless sneeze, or a few strands of hair might fall to the soil and be swiftly forgotten. When a horror like Charg brushes close to reality, the _vile remnants_ cast off from his nightmare form are not so harmless. At other times, the desecrated remains of innocent creatures can be transformed into _vile remnants_ as well. Worshippers of unholy gods and followers of evil philosophies gather these things and covet them as one might the hem of a cloak brushed against an idolized hero, or the visage of a divinity made manifest in a patch of mold on a wall. _Vile remnants_ spread fear and cruelty wherever they’re [hidden](/Conditions.aspx?ID=79) and can corrupt those who discover them. They might be buried in the soil of a farmer’s field, dropped into the depths of a village well, or stashed at the bottom of a toy box. Wherever the innocent might stumble across them and become unknowing actors in the decay of morality, the _vile remnant_ works its unholy magic. A _vile remnant_ appears as a raw, decaying mass of flesh, fur, and gristle—a teratoma consisting of warty skin, sightless eyes, a finger or a toe, tufts of bristly hair, or teeth without mouths or lips to hide them. Each _vile remnant’s_ shape is wildly different and uniquely unsettling. A _vile remnant_ automatically imparts to a PC the knowledge of how to use its Hear My Words activation as soon as it’s touched, but its other activations must be discovered normally through the use of Identify Magic (and as normal, identifying the presence and effect of the curse it carries requires a critical success at such an attempt). Unlike most cursed items, a character can discard a _vile remnant_, yet doing so runs a real risk that it might thereafter fall into the wrong hands. In this Adventure Path, any _vile remnant_ the PCs discard anywhere other than the restored reliquary in the Maiserene Church at area **A9** is discovered by one of the monsters of Bastardhall, who then [Hides](/Actions.aspx?ID=2404) the horror somewhere in the region where it was found. Where the horror is hidden is left to you to decide. As long as a creature carries a _vile remnant_, its thoughts and dreams are influenced by cruel notions and temptations to commit violent depravities. A creature that’s already predisposed toward these acts derives greater pleasure than before for such atrocities but receives no additional penalty or benefit, while a non-sapient creature is driven to become unnaturally violent in its actions (and over the course of weeks, becomes visibly corrupted by patches of strange fur, warty growths, unsightly teeth, or similar teratomas on its body). A sapient creature that isn’t predisposed toward acts of depravity (likely including all PCs) takes an item penalty equal to the number of _vile remnants_ they carry to saving throws against all magical effects that attempt to encourage such acts. Saving throws against spells like _suggestion_ or _charm_ cast by creatures who attempt to push a PC into such acts, any affect by such creatures that attempts to control a PC, or certain specific effects mentioned in the text of this adventure would all be affected by this penalty. A creature with the [holy](/Traits.aspx?ID=517) trait reduces the overall item penalty imparted by this curse by 1, to a minimum penalty of 0. A creature that’s foolish enough to consume a _vile remnant_ becomes fused to its curse, at which point the _vile remnant_ remains lodged within the creature’s body until the curse is removed from the creature with a _cleanse affliction_ spell or similar magic, or upon the creature’s death, whichever comes first. At this point, the _vile remnant_ crawls or oozes its way out of the creature’s body and flops, once again inanimate, onto the ground, where it waits to be claimed by a new carrier. As long as you carry a _vile remnant_ somewhere on your person, its curse does have a beneficial side: The power of its influence grants you a +1 item bonus to all saving throws against curses from other sources, as the _vile remnant_ jealously wards against such encroachments on its territory. Unlike the item penalty, carrying multiple _vile remnants_ does not increase this item bonus. The base version of a _vile remnant_ appears to be lifeless, but the _whispering remnant_ periodically twitches and pulses as if it were alive. **Activate—Become As One** 1 minute ([concentrate](/Traits.aspx?ID=561), [manipulate](/Traits.aspx?ID=645)) **Effect** By piling eight _vile remnants_ in a heap and then concentrating upon the mound of cursed flesh for a minute, you cause the eight _vile remnants_ to slither together and become a single _whispering remnant_. Once combined in this manner, the resulting _whispering remnant_ cannot be thereafter split into individual _vile remnants_. **Activate—Hear My Words** ([concentrate](/Traits.aspx?ID=561), [manipulate](/Traits.aspx?ID=645)) **Frequency** once per day; **Effect** The _vile remnant_ casts a DC 23 _enthrall_ spell to your specifications. Creatures that fail or critically fail to resist this spell perceive and remember the _vile remnant_ in your hand as something commonplace to the region, such as a farming tool, book, or fresh-baked pie, for as long as they remain enthralled. If you don’t take advantage of this to subtly guide any affected creatures toward undermining their society, the _vile remnant_ can’t be activated to Hear My Words again by you for 1 week. Additionally, the next time you sleep, you endure horrific nightmares and must succeed at a DC 23 Will save upon waking to avoid becoming [stupefied](/Conditions.aspx?ID=94) 1 for 24 hours (this is a mental effect). **Activate—Hide the Horror** 10 minutes ([manipulate](/Traits.aspx?ID=645)) **Frequency** once per year; **Effect** You hide the _vile remnant_ somewhere that, in time, it is likely to be found. For the following four weeks, _the vile remnant_’s evil seeps into the surrounding landscape, expanding its influence at a rate of 200 feet per day until it reaches its maximum emanation of 5,600 feet after 28 days. It continues to influence this area for another three weeks before going dormant— it must be recovered and rehidden later once this activation recharges to begin the cycle again. While the remnant’s influence is active, any sapient creature that sleeps in the area experiences unsettling dreams of being stalked by monsters they can never quite see or evade. A creature that doesn’t worship an unholy deity who experiences these dreams must succeed at a DC 23 Will save each time they rest to avoid awakening [fatigued](/Conditions.aspx?ID=73). On a critical failure, the creature awakens [stupefied](/Conditions.aspx?ID=94) 1 as well; this condition remains until removed or until they are no longer fatigued, whichever comes first. Creatures who worship an unholy deity or follow a despicable philosophy are immune to this effect. Any skill checks made by such creatures when performing rituals performed in the affected area gain a +1 item bonus, and _nightmare_ spells cast by them within the region have their save DCs increased by 1. **Destruction** A _vile remnant_ can’t be destroyed, but a _whispering remnant_ can be by hurling it into a powerful curse effect created by the deity associated with the remnant. This causes the _whispering remnant_ to become reabsorbed into the deity’s otherworldly body and often has potent side effects on the surrounding region. Disposing of a _whispering remnant_ in the soul vortex of Bastardhall (area
**I**) after Caydserris has been defeated not only destroys the _whispering remnant_ but helps bring the Bastardhall Curse to an end. Vile Remnant **Source** [Pathfinder #224: Bastion of Blasphemies](/Sources.aspx?ID=357) pg. 238 **Bulk** L Whispering Remnant **Source** [Pathfinder #224: Bastion of Blasphemies](/Sources.aspx?ID=357) pg. 238 **Bulk** L --- A _whispering remnant’s_ Hide the Horror aura expands at a rate of 500 feet per day for 28 days, and the DC’s for its Hear My Words and [Hide](/Actions.aspx?ID=2404) the Horror activations increase to 30. It imparts a -9 item penalty to all saving throws against deplorable influences and a +3 item bonus to all saving throws against curses as long as it’s carried. _Whispering remnants_ are incredibly rare, and their use is required in many vile rites, such as the one that brought down the curse on Castle Arudora. A _whispering remnant_ gains the following additional activation. **Activate—Heed My Whispers** ([concentrate](/Traits.aspx?ID=561), [manipulate](/Traits.aspx?ID=645)) **Frequency** once per day; **Effect** The _whispering remnant_ casts a DC 30 [_subconscious suggestion_](/Spells.aspx?ID=1692) spell to your specifications. If the target of the spell fails or critically fails to save against this, they perceive and remember the _whispering remnant_ as being a commonplace item. If you don’t suggest a course of action to the target that causes them to work at undermining their society, the _whispering remnant_ shrieks horribly, but only in your mind—you take 10d6 mental damage (DC 30 [basic](/Rules.aspx?ID=2297) Will save), after which the _whispering remnant_ cannot be activated again by you for 1 week.

This _+1 [striking](/Equipment.aspx?ID=280) [whip](/Weapons.aspx?ID=48)_ is crafted from the vine of a dangerous plant creature. [Violet Ray](/Equipment.aspx?ID=1139)
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Rare" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=137" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Guns & Gears (Remastered)](/Sources.aspx?ID=98) pg. 83

**Price** 1,893 gp

<row gap="medium">

**Usage** held in 2 hands

**Bulk** 2
</row>

<row gap="medium">

 

 

 
</row>

</column>

---

One of the many wondrous devices brought into the world by Stasian technology is the seemingly miraculous violet ray. Physicians claim it anything from headaches to heartburn, or nausea to deafness, all with an easy and painless treatment. The device is a glass vacuum with an insulated handle connected to a small Stasian coil. When powered, the glass tube fills with purple light and becomes warm to the touch. Pressing the tube to one's body is said to increase blood flow, eliminate toxins, and many other beneficial effects. A violet ray functions as a set of [healer's tools](/Equipment.aspx?ID=25) and provides a +2 item bonus to [Medicine](/Skills.aspx?ID=9) checks to [Administer First Aid](/Actions.aspx?ID=54), [Treat Disease](/Actions.aspx?ID=55), [Treat Poison](/Actions.aspx?ID=56), or [Treat Wounds](/Actions.aspx?ID=57).

**Activate** <actions string="Three Actions" /> ([manipulate](/Traits.aspx?ID=645)) **Frequency** once per day;   **Effect** You apply the violet ray to an adjacent creature and attempt to counteract the [blinded](/Conditions.aspx?ID=1), [clumsy](/Conditions.aspx?ID=3), [confused](/Conditions.aspx?ID=5), [deafened](/Conditions.aspx?ID=8), [drained](/Conditions.aspx?ID=10), [enfeebled](/Conditions.aspx?ID=13), [sickened](/Conditions.aspx?ID=34), or [stupefied](/Conditions.aspx?ID=37) condition with a [counteract](/Rules.aspx?ID=371) level of 6 and a counteract modifier of +22, using the source of the condition to determine the condition's counteract level and DC. If the condition was caused by an ongoing effect and you don't remove that effect, the condition returns after 1 minute. Each use of this ability can only counteract a single condition.

<column gap="tiny">

</column>

>
[Violin of the Waves](/Equipment.aspx?ID=2199)
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Uncommon" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=159" />
<trait label="Auditory" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=16" />
<trait label="Magical" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=103" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Treasure Vault (Remastered)](/Sources.aspx?ID=191) pg. 116

**Price** 700 gp

<row gap="medium">

**Usage** held in 2 hands

**Bulk** 1
</row>

<row gap="medium">

 

 

 
</row>

</column>

---

This violin is crafted from finely wrought rosewood that emits a strong, but pleasant, smell of salt water and ocean life. It's engraved with images of sailors working and waves gently rolling. When you make a [Performance](/Skills.aspx?ID=12) check using the _violin of the waves_, you gain a +2 item bonus to the check. This bonus increases to +3 if the performer is currently aboard a ship, walking on the ocean, or otherwise immediately adjacent to ocean water.

 The violin was created to play a specific tune, one that springs instantly into the mind of anyone who so much as casually strums the instrument. It's a tune of calm waters and safety, but also of pranks played upon shipmates and revelry.

**Activate** <actions string="" /> 5 minutes ([manipulate](/Traits.aspx?ID=645)) **Frequency** once per day;  **Requirements** You must be aboard a ship; **Effect** You play the song. Once it's completed, the weather immediately calms to the normal as it would for the season, as [control weather](/Rituals.aspx?ID=9). For the next day, the weather remains in this state, unless affected by other magical effects. Anyone aboard the ship finds their mind wanders when performing tasks however, daydreaming of drunken revelry or other forms of entertainment, and the crew of the ship takes a –2 status penalty to skill checks to do anything other than participate in such revelry.

<column gap="tiny">

</column>

    level="1"
    right="Item 4"

>
[Viper Arrow](/Equipment.aspx?ID=171)
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Conjuration" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=33" />
<trait label="Consumable" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=36" />
<trait label="Magical" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=103" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Core Rulebook](/Sources.aspx?ID=1) pg. 561

**Price** 17 gp

<row gap="medium">
**Ammunition** [arrow](/Weapons.aspx?ID=83)

</row>

<row gap="medium">
<row gap="tiny"><row>**Activate**</row><actions string="Single Action" /><row>command</row></row>

 

 

 
</row>

</column>

---

The shaft of this arrow is covered in fine green scales, and its iron head comes to a pair of points almost like fangs. After an activated _viper arrow_ hits a target, the arrow transforms into a [viper](/Monsters.aspx?ID=379). The target is affected by the viper's poison, as if it had been bitten. The viper then lands in an open space adjacent to the target.

 The viper has the [summoned](/Traits.aspx?ID=154) trait and acts at the end of your turn, even though you didn't use the Sustain a Spell action. It is under the GM's control, but it generally attacks the creature the arrow struck. The viper vanishes after 1 minute or when slain.

**Craft Requirements** Supply one casting of [_summon animal_](/Spells.aspx?ID=316).

</column>

>
[Viper Rapier](/Equipment.aspx?ID=2145)
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Apex" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=10" />
<trait label="Invested" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=98" />
<trait label="Magical" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=103" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Treasure Vault (Remastered)](/Sources.aspx?ID=191) pg. 104

**Price** 70,000 gp

<row gap="medium">

**Usage** held in 1 hand

**Bulk** 1
</row>

<row gap="medium">
**Base Weapon** [Rapier](/Weapons.aspx?ID=36)
</row>

<row gap="medium">

 

 

 
</row>

</column>

---

Crafted from flawless jade, the guard of this [rapier](/Weapons.aspx?ID=36) takes the form of a twisting serpent with the blade thrusting from its open mouth. This rapier functions as a _+3 [greater striking](/Equipment.aspx?ID=280) [quickstrike](/Equipment.aspx?ID=2844) rapier_. While wielding the rapier, your movement doesn't trigger reactions when you Stride, [Balance](/Actions.aspx?ID=28), or [Tumble Through](/Actions.aspx?ID=29). When you invest the rapier, you either increase your Dexterity modifier by 1 or increase it to +4, whichever would give you a higher value.

**Activate** <actions string="Reaction" /> ([concentrate](/Traits.aspx?ID=561)) **Frequency** once per day; **Trigger** You fail, but don't critically fail, an attack using the _viper rapier_;  **Effect** The tip of the rapier briefly takes the form of a viper's head, and the blade twists and contorts, biting the target you missed. The target is affected as if successfully poisoned with [cave worm venom](/Equipment.aspx?ID=3328) (DC 43).

**Activate** <actions string="Reaction" /> ([concentrate](/Traits.aspx?ID=561))  **Trigger** A creature misses or critically misses you with an attack;  **Effect** With a slight, obviously mocking bow or curtsy, you Step.

**Activate** <actions string="Two Actions" /> ([manipulate](/Traits.aspx?ID=645)) **Frequency** once per hour;   **Effect** You twirl your rapier in a serpentine pattern, causing your form to become a blur of motion. You're [concealed](/Conditions.aspx?ID=4) for 1 minute or until you take a [hostile action](/Rules.aspx?ID=300). While you're concealed, you also gain a +2 circumstance bonus to Reflex saving throws.

<column gap="tiny">

</column>

    level="1"
    right="Item 14"
    pfs="Standard"
>
[Viper's Fang](/Equipment.aspx?ID=238)
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Consumable" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=36" />
<trait label="Evocation" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=65" />
<trait label="Magical" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=103" />
<trait label="Talisman" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=155" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Core Rulebook](/Sources.aspx?ID=1) pg. 569

**Price** 850 gp

<row gap="medium">

**Usage** affixed to a weapon

</row>

<row gap="medium">
<row gap="tiny"><row>**Activate**</row><actions string="Reaction" /><row>envision</row></row>

 

**Trigger** A creature within your reach uses a manipulate or move action, makes a ranged attack, or leaves a square during a moving action it's using

**Requirement** You are a master with the affixed weapon
</row>

</column>

---

When you activate this resin-strengthened viper skull, you make an [Attack of Opportunity](/Actions.aspx?ID=8) against the triggering creature.

**Requirement** You are a master with the affixed weapon
</row>

---

When you activate this resin-strengthened viper skull, make a melee Strike against the triggering creature. If you have Reactive Strike, you can activate the viper's fang as a free action. If your attack is a critical hit and the trigger was a manipulate action, you disrupt that action. This Strike doesn't count toward your multiple attack penalty, and your multiple attack penalty doesn't apply to this Strike. If you hit with this attack, the creature is exposed to viper fang venom.

 **Viper Fang Venom** ([poison](/Traits.aspx?ID=126)); **Saving Throw** Fortitude DC 32; **Maximum Duration** 4 rounds; **Stage 1** 3d10 poison damage and [enfeebled](/Conditions.aspx?ID=13) 1.

</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Alchemical" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=528" />
<trait label="Consumable" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=564" />
<trait label="Elixir" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=589" />
<trait label="Morph" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=657" />
<trait label="Poison" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=669" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Howl of the Wild](/Sources.aspx?ID=226) pg. 111

<row gap="medium">

**Usage** held in 1 hand

**Bulk** L
</row>

<row gap="medium">
<row gap="tiny"><row>**Activate**</row><actions string="Single Action" /><row>([manipulate](/Traits.aspx?ID=645))</row></row>

 

 

 
</row>

</column>

---

Your teeth elongate into fangs with grooves that can channel a deadly venom. You gain a fangs unarmed attack that deals 1d6 piercing damage, unless you already have an unarmed bite attack that deals more damage. You gain the listed item bonus to unarmed attack and damage rolls when you [Strike](/Actions.aspx?ID=2306) with your fangs or another bite attack.

<column gap="tiny">

</column>

<row gap="medium">

</row>

</column>

</traits>

<row gap="medium">

</row>

</column>

---

<title
    level="1"
    right="Item 20"
    pfs="Limited"
>
[Viridian Crown](/Equipment.aspx?ID=3760)
</title>

<spoilers>May contain spoilers from Spore War</spoilers>

<traits>
<trait label="Unique" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=161" />
<trait label="Apex" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=10" />
<trait label="Artifact" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=253" />
<trait label="Invested" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=98" />
<trait label="Primal" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=134" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Pathfinder #212: A Voice in the Blight](/Sources.aspx?ID=255) pg. 77

<row gap="medium">

**Usage** worn headwear

**Bulk** L
</row>

<row gap="medium">

 

 

 
</row>

</column>

---

The monarch of Kyonin imparts a sliver of their personality to the artifact when they are crowned ruler of the nation. The crown’s precise shape changes with their needs. A paranoid ruler might cause the crown to transform into a cowl, while a gregarious one could cause it to become a lofty piece that displays its beauty.

Atop Queen Telandia’s brow, the _Viridian Crown_ has assumed its current appearance: brimming with life, its blue-green vines moving and rustling on her brow. While the material that comprises the crown seems to be made of living vines, to the touch it is as resilient as dawnsilver. In the spring, buds bloom into crystalline flowers that give the crown a scintillating appearance. These delicate flower petals naturally fall over time as the season advances, and often serve as temporary tokens or gifts to citizens and dignitaries. The petals are art objects worth a few dozen gp each, but the act of selling them is considered crass by Kyonin’s people–and their fragility ensures that they crumble to dust before too long anyway. Their use as raw materials in the crafting of consumable magic is a timehonored tradition among elves.

If you are the properly anointed ruler of Kyonin, or if that ruler has given you permission to wear the crown for a time, as long as you have the _Viridian Crown_ invested, choose either Charisma or Wisdom. The _Viridian Crown_ increases the chosen modifier by 1 or increases it to +4, whichever would give you a higher value. You can change which modifier is adjusted once every 24 hours as you make your daily preparations.

As long as you have the crown invested, it imparts knowledge of the [fortifying brew](/Rituals.aspx?ID=147) and [resurrect](/Rituals.aspx?ID=123) rituals. When you cast either of these (either as a primary or secondary caster) you gain a +3 item bonus to your skill check.

**Activate—Invoke the Crown** <actions string="" /> [Cast a Spell](/Actions.aspx?ID=2734) **Frequency** once per minute;   **Effect** You cast one of the following spells from the crown at 10th-rank: [_cleanse affliction_](/Spells.aspx?ID=1467), [_detect poison_](/Spells.aspx?ID=1486), [_heal_](/Spells.aspx?ID=1554), or [_light_](/Spells.aspx?ID=1585).

**Activate—View Subject** <actions string="" /> ([concentrate](/Traits.aspx?ID=561))    **Effect** You focus your thoughts, and the _Viridian Crown_ shows you an image of an elf who has accepted your rule. You must know the elf’s name or have met them in person. This functions as if the _Viridian Crown_ cast [_scrying_](/Spells.aspx?ID=1662) to your specifications. The target can resist the [scrying](/Traits.aspx?ID=689) effect with a DC 43 Will save if they wish.

**Activate—Elven Hope** <actions string="Single Action" /> ([concentrate](/Traits.aspx?ID=561), [emotion](/Traits.aspx?ID=590), [mental](/Traits.aspx?ID=647)) **Frequency** once per hour;   **Effect** You draw upon the hope of the elven people, and exude these positive thoughts in a 60-foot [emanation](/Rules.aspx?ID=2387). You and all allies in this area gain a +3 status bonus to saving throws against [mental](/Traits.aspx?ID=647) effects. You can [Sustain](/Actions.aspx?ID=2317) this Activation for up to 1 minute.

**Activate—Garden Sanctuary** <actions string="Two Actions" /> ([concentrate](/Traits.aspx?ID=561), [manipulate](/Traits.aspx?ID=645)) **Frequency** three times per day;   **Effect** You touch the _Viridian Crown_, then pass your hand outward, palm down. A glorious and beautiful garden blossoms around you in a 30-foot [emanation](/Rules.aspx?ID=2387). The plants comprising this garden are of a type appropriate to the terrain, but if no plants are appropriate, you can choose the type. The garden’s plants actively move and twist to oppose passage by your enemies, and they treat the terrain as greater [difficult terrain](/Rules.aspx?ID=2366). As long as you begin your turn in the garden sanctuary, it gains the minion trait and can use its two actions to cast spells at your direction. The garden sanctuary’s spells are cast at 9th-rank, and it has 3 spell slots to cast spells each day. It can cast [_field of life_](/Spells.aspx?ID=1526), [_moment of renewal_](/Spells.aspx?ID=1607), or [_tree of seasons_](/Spells.aspx?ID=1725), treating its center as the point of origin for these spells as needed. The garden sanctuary persists until you use this activation again.

**Destruction** The _Viridian Crown_ withers and dies if a rightfully coronated monarch pledges the crown to a [demon](/MonsterFamilies.aspx?ID=387) lord during a ritual that takes 24 hours to complete.

<column gap="tiny">

</column>

---

Life-infused soil from the [Plane of Earth](/Planes.aspx?ID=5), _vital earth_ is glittering dust you inhale that causes you to not need air or water for 24 hours. Also, for this time, your wounds close easily, like molding clay, meaning someone attempting to [Administer First Aid](/Actions.aspx?ID=54) or [Treat Wounds](/Actions.aspx?ID=57) on you doesn't need a [healer's toolkit](/Equipment.aspx?ID=25) and gains a +1 item bonus to the [Medicine](/Skills.aspx?ID=9) check.

>
[Vocal Shells](/Equipment.aspx?ID=3526)
</title>

<spoilers>May contain spoilers from Convocation</spoilers>

<traits>
<trait label="Rare" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=683" />
<trait label="Clockwork" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=331" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Rival Academies](/Sources.aspx?ID=235) pg. 54

**Price** 50 gp (set of two)

<row gap="medium">

</row>

<row gap="medium">

 

 

 
</row>

</column>

---

Used by more technologically inclined bards, ventriloquists, and other performers to throw their voices, this gadget consists of two button-sized conch shells, each containing a miniaturized mechanism designed to pick up and transmit sound. One of the shells is designated the sending shell and contains a tiny indentation. When this indentation is pressed and the shell is close to a source of sound (such as on an actor's necklace), any sound that reaches it is transmitted to the receiver shell. If the receiver shell is located within 20 feet, it plays the sounds captured by the sending shell at a perfect volume and pitch.

<title
    level="1"
    right="Item 13"
    pfs="Restricted"
>
[Void Fragment](/Equipment.aspx?ID=2373)
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Rare" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=137" />
<trait label="Consumable" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=36" />
<trait label="Occult" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=120" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Treasure Vault (Remastered)](/Sources.aspx?ID=191) pg. 189

<row gap="medium">

**Usage** touched

</row>

<row gap="medium">
<row gap="tiny"><row>**Activate**</row><actions string="Single Action" /><row>([manipulate](/Traits.aspx?ID=104))</row></row>

 

 

 
</row>

</column>

---

Hovering midair, thrumming and whispering of its power, a _void fragment_ is a crystalline fragment of swirling colors, reminiscent of stars and deep darkness. It thrums intermittently with a beckoning vibration, drawing attention from and pulling at nearby creatures with a tangible sense of gravity. A chill hangs in the air around it. At a touch, the wisp vanishes, giving the point of contact a gangrenous color. If the partaker succeeds at the initial save, the wisp reappears somewhere on the same planet.

---

**Stage 1 (8 Days)** The first time you enter this stage from a given void fragment, you gain the effect of a [_potion of truespeech_](/Equipment.aspx?ID=2954) for 3 days. The wisp grants you [telepathy](/MonsterAbilities.aspx?ID=37) with a range of 30 feet. Also, you are under the effects of [_hidden mind_](/Spells.aspx?ID=1556), except that its status bonus is +1 and it [counteracts](/Rules.aspx?ID=371) with a bonus equal to your class DC – 9. The wisp grants you resistance to [mental](/Traits.aspx?ID=106) damage equal to half your level. You also have access to the following activation.

**Activate** <actions string="" /> <actions string="Single Action" /> or <actions string="Two Actions" /> ([concentrate](/Traits.aspx?ID=561), [teleportation](/Traits.aspx?ID=710)) **Frequency** once per hour;   **Effect** You teleport up to 30 feet to an unoccupied space you can see. If you used 2 actions, you can teleport up to 60 feet.

---

**Stage 2 (24 Days)** You gain [imprecise](/Rules.aspx?ID=412) thoughtsense to half your telepathy's range, which increases to 60 feet. However, you have a tough time filtering the mental noise. If any creatures can be detected by your thoughtsense, you take a –1 penalty to Perception checks. When you arrive in a space after using the activation to teleport, you create a 10-foot emanation that works like [_strange geometry_](/Spells.aspx?ID=719)  for 1 round. This emanation can affect you.

 If you die at this stage or higher, your body implodes. Your soul reincarnates as an [aberration](/Traits.aspx?ID=1) of a level close to yours, which extrudes from the location of your implosion. Common forms include [jah-tohl](/Monsters.aspx?ID=2930), [gosreg](/Monsters.aspx?ID=2931), [quelaunt](/Monsters.aspx?ID=3159), [rhu-chalik](/Monsters.aspx?ID=2928), [shoggoth](/Monsters.aspx?ID=368), and [xoarian](/Monsters.aspx?ID=2929). This creature isn't you, but fleeting memories of your former existence remain with it. You can't be raised from the dead while this monster endures. The _void fragment_ reappears somewhere on the same planet.

---

**Stage 3 (32 Days)** Your telepathy range increases to 100 feet, and the wisp grants you resistance to [mental](/Traits.aspx?ID=106) damage equal to your level. The mental noise increases the penalty to Perception to –2. Whenever you roll initiative, you become confused for up to 1d4 rounds.

---

**Stage 4** You die.

---

 **Purging** You must find and slay a powerful [aberration](/Traits.aspx?ID=523) or a servant of such creatures the GM deems appropriate. The creature must be of your level or higher. Then, someone must cast a [_rest eternal_](/Rituals.aspx?ID=153) ritual on you and the dead being; you must be anointed with the same oils the ritual normally requires. If the ritual results in a success, it casts the slain creature into the void along with the _void fragment_ inside you, ending its effects on you.

<column gap="tiny">

</column>

May contain spoilers from Malevolence **Source** [Malevolence](/Sources.aspx?ID=88) pg. 68 **Usage** mounted in frame (see below) **Bulk** 3 --- The _Void Mirror_ was created on a distant planet by a now-extinct alien cult to aid in unlocking the secrets of the Dark Tapestry. It appears as a 5-foot-tall, 2-foot-wide mirror of dark glass. As long as it's unmounted in a frame, the _Void Mirror_ functions only as a mirror, save that it always reflects the sky as if it were night, regardless of the time of day. When the _Void Mirror_ is mounted in a frame, it instead serves as a window into space, displaying a star field in its glass rather than a reflection. This frame can be of any quality, but stouter frames help to prevent the frame's destruction and thus help to keep the _Void Mirror_ functional. The view presented by the _Void Mirror_ is any view of the night sky possible from its current physical location, regardless of time of day. Observations of the sky in this way add a +3 item bonus to [Astronomy Lore](/Skills.aspx?ID=8) or Perception checks made while using the mirror. The point of view can be shifted through hand gestures, causing the scene within the mirror to reorient in any direction desired. A character who peers into the starscape within the _Void Mirror_ must attempt a DC 41 Will save. On a failure, the character feels something looking back at them from the dark places between the stars. On a critical failure, this sensation causes the character to become [frightened 1](/Conditions.aspx?ID=19). The character is then temporarily immune to this effect for 24 hours. By placing the _Void Mirror_ in a specially-constructed frame (such as the one within the Cosmic Crypt in this adventure), it can halt the ongoing transformation of a creature that has performed the apotheosis activation. Building such a frame is beyond the skill of low-level characters, as it requires an artisan with legendary proficiency in [Crafting](/Skills.aspx?ID=4). The _Void Mirror_ can be utilized in other ways, but before a character can activate these effects the occult methods to access these ritual-like effects must be [Researched](/Rules.aspx?ID=1205) separately. Since the specific methods for these activations vary slightly from person to person, these methods can't be taught; each person who seeks to activate the _Void Mirror_ in one of the following ways must complete their own research to unlock the artifact's secrets. Each requires a separate number of [Occultism](/Skills.aspx?ID=11) checks to Research, as detailed below for each activation. **Activate** 1 hour (Intract); **Research** Accumulate 12 RP by making DC 20 Occultism (expert) checks when Researching (1 week per attempt); **Frequency** once per month; **Effect** The first activation ritual is known as “Speak to the Void” and allows the user to contact an intelligence in a distant part of the universe, provided the mirror shows that location (regardless of distance). This alien intelligence infuses the user's mind with answers, allowing the user to [Recall Knowledge](/Actions.aspx?ID=26) using [Nature](/Domains.aspx?ID=22) or [Occultism](/Skills.aspx?ID=11) as if they were legendary proficiency with the skill (including the +8 proficiency bonus). If this check fails, the character takes 10d6 mental damage (100 mental damage on a critical failure) as the imparted knowledge does more harm than good. **Activate** 1 hour (Interact); **Research** Accumulate 12 RP by making DC 30 Occultism (master) checks when Researching (1 month per attempt); **Frequency** once per year; **Effect** The second activation ritual is known as “Call from the Void.” The user performs a 1-hour-long rite before the _Void Mirror_, during which they indicate a type of [aberration](/Traits.aspx?ID=1), [beast](/Traits.aspx?ID=20), [fungus](/Traits.aspx?ID=77), [ooze](/Traits.aspx?ID=122), or [plant](/Traits.aspx?ID=125) creature that's an alien life form from the planet the user is currently located on. The target creature must be a level equal to or less than the user's level +4. As the rite ends, the user attempts an Occultism check against the target creature's Will DC. **Critical Success** The creature is drawn across the universe to appear in a space adjacent to the _Void Mirror_. The creature's initial attitude toward the user is [helpful](/Conditions.aspx?ID=21), but this attitude can shift quickly if the creature realizes its goals and personality differs dramatically from the user's, or if the user makes a request of the creature that's against its nature. As long both the creature and the user are within 30 feet of the _Void Mirror_, the user can return the creature to its original location by Dismissing this activation. The creature can attempt a Will save against the user's Occultism DC to resist being returned; if it succeeds, it's temporarily immune for 24 hours.
**Success** As critical success, but the creature is [indifferent](/Conditions.aspx?ID=25) upon arrival.
**Failure** As critical success, but the creature is [hostile](/Conditions.aspx?ID=23) upon arrival.
**Critical Failure** As failure, but magical feedback from the failed activation causes the user to become [stunned 3](/Conditions.aspx?ID=36). **Activate** 7 days (Interact); **Research** Accumulate 12 RP by making DC 40 Occultism (legendary) checks when Researching (1 year per attempt); **Frequency** once per century; **Effect** The third activation ritual is known as “Become the Void” and requires the user to continue performing the rite for 7 consecutive days (as if they were performing a multi-day ritual). If the user fails to perform this rite for one of these 7 consecutive days, they immediately suffer the critical failure effect below. **Critical Success** The user's body, mind, and soul are infused with alien energies drawn from the Dark Tapestry, which transforms the user into an [aberration](/Traits.aspx?ID=1) of a level no higher than their current level +4. This new form could be an existing aberration or a unique one of the GM's creation. The user retains their memories and spellcasting ability (including any rituals they know) but becomes chaotic evil and loses all other abilities they possessed in their previous form.
**Success** As critical success, but the aberration the user transforms into can be of a level no higher than half the user's current level.
**Failure** The user's attempt to change is a painful mistake that deals 10d6+40 bludgeoning damage as their body twists, bends and breaks. Ultimately, they are not transformed.
**Critical Failure** The user is slain, but their body shifts and transforms into a brand new creature as the bodiless alien intelligence Tchekuth incubates within the user's flesh, mind and soul. This transformation takes another 7 days to complete but can be halted indefinitely if the _Void Mirror_ is placed in a specially constructed frame aimed at the body's location (regardless of any solid object between the mirror and the body). Slowing or stopping this transformation via other means requires complex rituals or divine intervention, subject to the GM's whim. After 7 days, the body completes its transformation and Tchekuth rises once more as a physical threat. **Destruction** A creature that completes the apotheosis of Becoming the Void can destroy the _Void Mirror_ by smashing it, though doing so also destroys the creature performing this action in a violent burst of occult energy

May contain spoilers from Spore War **Source** [Pathfinder #212: A Voice in the Blight](/Sources.aspx?ID=255) pg. 79 **Price** 12,500 gp **Usage** held in 2 hands --- _Void shackles_ are built from supernatural crystals that form in the Void—materials that dig painfully into the flesh of those they restrain. A set of void shackles functions as [superior manacles](/Equipment.aspx?ID=2733), but while they are in the Void, the crystals fluctuate in response to the plane’s energy, which increases all DCs to remove them or [Escape](/Actions.aspx?ID=2296) by 1 to DC 43. If a check to remove void shackles from a creature fails, the wearer of the manacles takes 10d6 [void](/Traits.aspx?ID=510) damage (DC 37 [basic](/Rules.aspx?ID=2297) Fortitude save). While a creature is manacled, the void shackles attempt to [counteract](/Rules.aspx?ID=2250) any [teleportation](/Traits.aspx?ID=710) effect that targets the manacled creature, with a counteract rank of 9th and a +25 modifier to the roll. If the teleportation effect is countered, the manacled creature takes 10d6 void damage (DC 37 basic Fortitude save). _Void shackles_ can be placed on [incorporeal](/Traits.aspx?ID=632) creatures as if they were not incorporeal. An incorporeal creature manacled by _void shackles_ cannot pass through solid objects. Even a soul can be restrained via _void shackles_, provided the soul was of a 17th- or lower-level creature in life. A soul held in _void shackles_ cannot move on to the afterlife, cannot become [undead](/Traits.aspx?ID=722), and can be transported by simply transporting the shackles. **Activate—Affix Shackle** ([manipulate](/Traits.aspx?ID=645)) **Effect** You affix the _void shackles_ to a helpless or willing creature or to any 17th- or lower-level soul. The shackles grow in size to accommodate the wrists or ankles of any size creature. **Activate—Release Shackle** ([manipulate](/Traits.aspx?ID=645)) **Effect** You cause the void shackles to open and release their prisoner. If you were not the one to affix the shackles to that creature or soul, you must attempt a DC 43 Will save. **Critical Success** The shackles open.
**Success** The shackles open, but you and the shackled creature take 5d6 [void](/Traits.aspx?ID=510) damage.
**Failure** The shackles do not open, and you and the shackled creature take 10d6 void damage.
**Critical Failure** As failure, but 20d6 void damage.

</title>

<traits>

<trait label="Magical" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=644" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [GM Core](/Sources.aspx?ID=218) pg. 239

**Price** 15,000 gp

<row gap="medium">

**Usage** etched onto a slashing melee weapon

</row>

<row gap="medium">

 

 

 
</row>

</column>

---

Originally created as a means of slaying the legendary jabberwock, _vorpal_ weapons prove equally effective against nearly any foe with a head. 

**Activate—Snicker-Snack** <actions string="Reaction" /> ([concentrate](/Actions.aspx?ID=683), [death](/Traits.aspx?ID=571), [incapacitation](/Traits.aspx?ID=93))   **Trigger** You roll a natural 20 on a Strike with the weapon against a creature that has a head, critically succeed, and deal slashing damage;  **Effect** The target must succeed at a DC 37 Fortitude save or be decapitated. This kills any creature except ones that don't require a head to live. For creatures with multiple heads, this usually kills the creature only if you sever its last head.

<title
    level="1"
    right="Item 6"
    pfs="Limited"
>
[Vortex Pouch](/Equipment.aspx?ID=3996)
</title>

<spoilers>May contain spoilers from Myth-Speaker</spoilers>

<traits>
<trait label="Rare" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=137" />
<trait label="Air" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=5" />
<trait label="Magical" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=103" />
<trait label="Mythic" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=835" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Pathfinder #217: Death Sails a Wine-Dark Sea
](/Sources.aspx?ID=273) pg. 78

**Price** 240 gp

<row gap="medium">

**Usage** held in 1 hand

</row>

<row gap="medium">

 

 

 
</row>

</column>

---

When empty, the _vortex pouch’s_ net seems too loose to hold much. However, when used to catch the wind, it stretches to hold the air. With nowhere for the wind to go, the air inside it swirls violently. If the caught wind includes a storm, clouds, [fog](/WeatherHazards.aspx?ID=4), or similar effect, it’s visible among the whirlwind.

**Activate—Catch Wind** <actions string="Two Actions" /> ([air](/Traits.aspx?ID=527), [manipulate](/Traits.aspx?ID=645))   **Requirements** The _vortex pouch_ is empty; **Effect** You gather the nearby air and wind within the _vortex pouch_. Creatures within a 20-foot [emanation](/Rules.aspx?ID=2387) must attempt a DC 20 Fortitude save or be moved 5 feet closer toward you as the air rushes into the pouch. Targets that critically fail the save are moved 10 feet. You can [Sustain](/Actions.aspx?ID=2317) the activation once per round, up to 1 minute, to continue Catching Wind. If you spend a [Mythic Point](/Rules.aspx?ID=3323) when Catching Wind, the vortex pouch gathers air in a 10-mile radius; though the vortex is only strong enough to forcibly suck in creatures within the original 20-foot emanation, weaker creatures with the air trait and creatures associated with the sky in the 10-mile radius will know your general direction and feel a sense of unease, granting you a +2 status bonus to [Intimidation](/Skills.aspx?ID=40) checks against those creatures for 1 week. When you end the activation, the vortex pouch becomes 1 Bulk and you can empty it using Release Wind.

**Activate—Release Wind** <actions string="Two Actions" /> ([air](/Traits.aspx?ID=527), [manipulate](/Traits.aspx?ID=645))   **Requirements** The _vortex pouch_ contains air or wind; **Effect** Wind rushes out of the _vortex pouch_ in a 30-foot [cone](/Rules.aspx?ID=2386). All creatures in the cone take 8d6 bludgeoning damage (DC 20 [basic](/Rules.aspx?ID=2297) Fortitude save). Creatures that fail their saving throw are pushed 5 feet away from you; creatures that critically fail are pushed 10 feet. If the caught wind included weather that might deal a different type of damage, Release Wind deals this damage instead (for instance, dealing [electricity](/Traits.aspx?ID=586) damage if it caught a thundercloud or [cold](/Traits.aspx?ID=555) damage if it caught a [blizzard](/WeatherHazards.aspx?ID=1)).

<column gap="tiny">

</column>

**Source** [GM Core](/Sources.aspx?ID=218) pg. 297 **Price** 14,800 gp **Usage** worn backpack --- This leather rucksack has icons burned into it, and every time it's taken to a plane it hasn't been to before, a new icon representing that plane scorches into the surface. The pack grants you a +3 bonus to Survival checks. It also enables you to see the magical traces of creatures' passage, allowing you to Track a creature that has teleported. The GM sets the DC of this check, usually using the spell DC or the level of the teleportation's caster. This lets you find the location of the creature's destination, and you can use that destination when casting teleport or activating the pack, even though you don't know what it looks like.
The pack contains an extradimensional space with the same properties as a type II _spacious pouch_. This space contains the contents of a climber's kit. If any components of that kit are removed and not returned, they return to the pack at dawn each day. **Activate—Group Voyage** 10 minutes ([concentrate](/Traits.aspx?ID=32), [manipulate](/Traits.aspx?ID=104)) **Effect** As you activate the pack, you can harness up to four willing creatures to the ropes on the pack. At the end of the activation time, the pack casts a 7th-rank [_interplanar teleport_](/Spells.aspx?ID=1576) or _teleport_ spell, transporting you and everyone attached to the pack. Attempt a DC 45 Survival check. On a success, you arrive 25 miles off target using _interplanar teleport_ or halve the distance you're off-target with _teleport_. On a critical success, you arrive exactly on target.

The pack grants you a +3 bonus to Survival checks. It also enables you to see the magical traces of creatures' passage, allowing you to Track a creature that has teleported. The GM sets the DC of this check, usually using the spell DC or the level of the teleportation's caster. This lets you find the location of the creature's destination, and you can use that destination when casting teleport or activating the pack, even though you don't know what it looks like. The pack contains an extradimensional space with the same properties as a type II spacious pouch . This space contains the contents of a climber's kit. If any components of that kit are removed and not returned, they return to the pack at dawn each day. Activate—Group Voyage 10 minutes (concentrate, manipulate) Effect As you activate the pack, you can harness up to four willing creatures to the ropes on the pack. At the end of the activation time, the pack casts a 7th-rank interplanar teleport or teleport spell, transporting you and everyone attached to the pack. Attempt a DC 45 Survival check. On a success, you arrive 25 miles off target using interplanar teleport or halve the distance you're off-target with teleport . On a critical success, you arrive exactly on target.

[Voyager's Pack](/Equipment.aspx?ID=469)
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Uncommon" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=159" />

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Core Rulebook](/Sources.aspx?ID=1) pg. 617

<row gap="medium">

**Usage** worn backpack

</row>

<row gap="medium">

 

 

 
</row>

</column>

---

This leather rucksack has icons burned into it, and every time it’s taken to a plane it hasn’t been to before, a new icon representing that plane scorches into the surface. The pack grants you a +3 bonus to Survival checks. It also enables you to see the magical traces of creatures’ passage, allowing you to Track a creature that has teleported. The GM sets the DC of this check, usually using the level and DC of the teleportation spell. This lets you find the location of the creature’s destination, and you can use that destination when casting [_teleport_](/Spells.aspx?ID=338) or activating the pack, even though you don’t know what it looks like.

 The pack contains an extradimensional space with the same properties as a [_type II bag of holding_](/Equipment.aspx?ID=249). This space contains the contents of a climber’s kit. If any components of that kit are removed and not returned, they return to the pack at dawn each day.

**Activate** <actions string="" /> 10 minutes (command, envision, Interact);     **Effect** As you activate the pack, you can harness up to four willing creatures to the ropes on the pack. At the end of the activation time, the pack casts a 7th-level [_plane shift_](/Spells.aspx?ID=222) or _teleport_ spell, transporting you and everyone attached to the pack. Attempt a DC 45 Survival check. On a success, you arrive 25 miles off target using _plane shift_ or halve the distance you’re off-target with _teleport_. On a critical success, you arrive exactly on target.

</column>

<traits>
<trait label="Uncommon" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=159" />
<trait label="Catalyst" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=396" />
<trait label="Consumable" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=36" />

</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Impossible Lands](/Sources.aspx?ID=146) pg. 178

**Price** 200 gp

<row gap="medium">

**Usage** held in 1 hand

**Bulk** L
</row>

**Access** Characters from Geb have access to this item.

<row gap="medium">
<row gap="tiny"><row>**Activate**</row><actions string="Single Action" /><row>Cast a Spell</row></row>

 

 

 
</row>

</column>

---

This fan of vulture feathers scatters on an unnatural gust of wind. If this catalyst is used to cast a [_ray of enfeeblement_](/Spells.aspx?ID=244) spell that has been heightened to at least 5th level, instead of targeting a single creature, you cast the spell in a 30-foot-area cone. You don't make a spell attack roll, instead affecting all creatures within the area with the effect the spell would normally have on a hit. This means creatures within the area must attempt a Fortitude save to determine whether they're [enfeebled](/Conditions.aspx?ID=13).

</column>

The plates of this waffle iron are made of [standard-grade mithral](/Equipment.aspx?ID=275) rather than iron and might bear an imprint on the plates. As with other mithral cookware, food rarely sticks to a mithral waffle iron. As it's made of mithral, this is an uncommon item.

<row gap="medium">

**Bulk** 1

---

Truly fit for emperors and demigods, this waffle iron is made of high-grade mithral. Although most metallurgists are certain that the much more affordable standard-grade mithral waffle iron maintains mithral's full non-stick properties, the super elite insist that only waffles made from high-grade mithral waffle irons conform to the most perfect shape and texture. Nadian has one high-grade mithral waffle iron for sale emblazoned with an archaic symbol associated with [Milani](/Deities.aspx?ID=43) from before she became a deity, supposedly used to make Milani herself waffles during her mortal life. As it's made of mithral, this is an uncommon item.

</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Pathfinder Special: Fumbus](/Sources.aspx?ID=105)

**Price** 160 gp

<row gap="medium">

**Usage** held in 1 hand

**Bulk** L
</row>

<row gap="medium">

 

 

 
</row>

</column>

---

This dirty metal wand is covered in an oily acrid smelling film. 

**Activate** <actions string="" /> Cast a Spell;  **Frequency** once per day, plus overcharge;   **Effect** You cast [_grease_](/Spells.aspx?ID=140), but the grease is caustic. If you cast this spell on an area, any creature that fails their Reflex save and falls [prone](/Conditions.aspx?ID=31), or that begins their turn prone, takes 1d6 acid damage. If you cast this spell on an unattended object, the first creature to pick up the object during the duration takes 1d6 [persistent acid damage](/Conditions.aspx?ID=29). If you cast this spell on an attended object and the holder or wielder fails their [Acrobatics](/Skills.aspx?ID=1) or Reflex save, the holder or wielder takes 1d6 persistent acid damage. <row gap="medium">

**Usage** held in 1 hand

**Bulk** L
</row>

<row gap="medium">

 

 

 
</row>

</column>

---

This intricately carved quartz wand changes color, cycling through the colors of the rainbow.

**Activate** <actions string="" /> Cast a Spell;  **Frequency** once per day, plus overcharge;   **Effect** You cast [_chromatic armor_](/Spells.aspx?ID=881) of the indicated level. Additionally, the target can use the Chromatic Armor Burst action.

**Chromatic Armor** Burst <actions string="Single Action" /> ([concentrate](/Traits.aspx?ID=561), [evocation](/Traits.aspx?ID=65), [light](/Traits.aspx?ID=640), [magical](/Traits.aspx?ID=644)); **Requirements** You’re affected by _chromatic armor_ created by the _wand of chromatic burst_; **Effect** Choose one color of the _chromatic armor_ the wand created for you. The spell ends and light of that color flashes brightly in a 20-foot [emanation](/Rules.aspx?ID=2387). Creatures in the area take damage of the type associated with the color you chose, with a [basic](/Rules.aspx?ID=2297) Reflex save against your spell DC; the amount of damage depends on the wand’s type. This action has the trait corresponding to the damage type you chose.

**Craft Requirements** Supply a casting of [_chromatic armor_](/Spells.aspx?ID=881) of the appropriate level.

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Treasure Vault (Remastered)](/Sources.aspx?ID=191) pg. 139

**Price** 160 gp

<row gap="medium">

**Usage** held in 1 hand

**Bulk** L
</row>

<row gap="medium">

 

 

 
</row>

</column>

---

Cracks and healed fractures spiderweb the shaft of this bone wand, worsening each time the wand is used. The bone's worn epiphysis forms the wand's pommel, and black leather wraps around the handle.

**Activate** <actions string="" /> Cast a Spell;  **Frequency** once per day, plus overcharge;   **Effect** You cast [_enfeeble_](/Spells.aspx?ID=1513). After you cast the spell, if the target is [enfeebled](/Conditions.aspx?ID=71), it releases a 10-foot [emanation](/Rules.aspx?ID=2387) that doesn’t include itself. Each creature in that area must attempt a Fortitude save as if targeted by enfeeble, but gets an outcome one degree of success better than it rolled.

**Craft Requirements** Supply a casting of _enfeeble_.

<title
    level="1"
    right="Item 4"
    pfs="Standard"
>
[Wand of Crushing Leaps](/Equipment.aspx?ID=2276)
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Magical" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=103" />
<trait label="Wand" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=164" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Treasure Vault (Remastered)](/Sources.aspx?ID=191) pg. 139

**Price** 80 gp

<row gap="medium">

**Usage** held in 1 hand

**Bulk** L
</row>

<row gap="medium">

 

 

 
</row>

</column>

---

This supple, light wooden wand drifts to the ground like a feather or leaf when dropped, landing unharmed. A thin coil of metal wraps around the wand's handle.

**Activate** <actions string="" /> Cast a Spell;  **Frequency** once per day, plus overcharge;   **Effect** You cast [_jump_](/Spells.aspx?ID=167), but can jump up to 60 feet. When you land you shatter the ground, making each creature in a 5-foot emanation [off-guard](/Conditions.aspx?ID=58) until the start of its next turn. In addition, the space you land in and all squares in the emanation become difficult terrain for 1 minute.

**Craft Requirements** Supply a casting of 1st-rank _jump_.

<column gap="tiny">

</column>

</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Fire" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=72" />
<trait label="Holy" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=517" />
<trait label="Light" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=100" />
<trait label="Magical" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=103" />
<trait label="Wand" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=164" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Treasure Vault (Remastered)](/Sources.aspx?ID=191) pg. 139

<row gap="medium">

**Usage** held in 1 hand

**Bulk** L
</row>

<row gap="medium">

 

 

 
</row>

</column>

---

Solidified radiance comprises this slender, featureless wand. It sheds [bright light](/Rules.aspx?ID=407) in a 20-foot radius and [dim light](/Rules.aspx?ID=408) for the next 20 feet. After you Activate the wand, the light fades, so it only sheds dim light in a 20-foot radius. The wand returns to its original brightness each dawn.

A creature that takes damage from the spell is [blinded](/Conditions.aspx?ID=59) for 1 round and [dazzled](/Conditions.aspx?ID=65) for a number of rounds equal to the spell rank. On a critical success on the attack roll, the target is also blinded for as long as it’s dazzled from the spell. However, it can attempt a Fortitude saving throw against your spell DC at the end of each of its turns, ending the blinded condition on a success (but remaining dazzled).

**Craft Requirements** Supply a casting of _holy light_ of the appropriate rank.

<trait label="Fire" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=72" />

**Usage** held in 1 hand

**Bulk** L
</row>

<row gap="medium">

 

 

 
</row>

</column>

---

Solidified radiance comprises this slender, featureless wand. It sheds [bright light](/Rules.aspx?ID=2402) in a 20-foot radius and [dim light](/Rules.aspx?ID=2403) for the next 20 feet. After you Activate the wand, the light fades, so it only sheds dim light in a 20-foot radius. The wand returns to its original brightness each dawn.

**Activate** <actions string="" /> Cast a Spell;  **Frequency** once per day, plus overcharge;   **Effect** You cast searing light of the indicated level, dazzling your target with the beam’s intensity. A creature that takes damage from the spell is [blinded](/Conditions.aspx?ID=59) for 1 round and [dazzled](/Conditions.aspx?ID=65) for a number of rounds equal to the spell level. On a critical success on the attack roll, the target is also blinded for as long as it’s dazzled from the spell. However, it can attempt a Fortitude saving throw against your spell DC at the end of each of its turns, ending the blinded condition on a success (but remaining dazzled).

**Craft Requirements** Supply a casting of [_searing light_](/Spells.aspx?ID=269) of the appropriate level.

Solidified radiance comprises this slender, featureless wand. It sheds [bright light](/Rules.aspx?ID=407) in a 20-foot radius and [dim light](/Rules.aspx?ID=408) for the next 20 feet. After you Activate the wand, the light fades, so it only sheds dim light in a 20-foot radius. The wand returns to its original brightness each dawn.

**Activate** <actions string="" /> Cast a Spell;  **Frequency** once per day, plus overcharge;   **Effect** You cast [_holy light_](/Spells.aspx?ID=1557) of the indicated rank, dazzling your target with the beam’s intensity. A creature that takes damage from the spell is [blinded](/Conditions.aspx?ID=59) for 1 round and [dazzled](/Conditions.aspx?ID=65) for a number of rounds equal to the spell rank. On a critical success on the attack roll, the target is also blinded for as long as it’s dazzled from the spell. However, it can attempt a Fortitude saving throw against your spell DC at the end of each of its turns, ending the blinded condition on a success (but remaining dazzled).

**Craft Requirements** Supply a casting of _holy light_ of the appropriate rank.

</row>

</row>

---

Solidified radiance comprises this slender, featureless wand. It sheds [bright light](/Rules.aspx?ID=407) in a 20-foot radius and [dim light](/Rules.aspx?ID=408) for the next 20 feet. After you Activate the wand, the light fades, so it only sheds dim light in a 20-foot radius. The wand returns to its original brightness each dawn.

**Activate** <actions string="" /> Cast a Spell;  **Frequency** once per day, plus overcharge;   **Effect** You cast [_holy light_](/Spells.aspx?ID=1557) of the indicated rank, dazzling your target with the beam’s intensity. A creature that takes damage from the spell is [blinded](/Conditions.aspx?ID=59) for 1 round and [dazzled](/Conditions.aspx?ID=65) for a number of rounds equal to the spell rank. On a critical success on the attack roll, the target is also blinded for as long as it’s dazzled from the spell. However, it can attempt a Fortitude saving throw against your spell DC at the end of each of its turns, ending the blinded condition on a success (but remaining dazzled).

**Craft Requirements** Supply a casting of _holy light_ of the appropriate rank.

---

Solidified radiance comprises this slender, featureless wand. It sheds [bright light](/Rules.aspx?ID=2402) in a 20-foot radius and [dim light](/Rules.aspx?ID=2403) for the next 20 feet. After you Activate the wand, the light fades, so it only sheds dim light in a 20-foot radius. The wand returns to its original brightness each dawn.

**Activate** <actions string="" /> Cast a Spell;  **Frequency** once per day, plus overcharge;   **Effect** You cast searing light of the indicated level, dazzling your target with the beam’s intensity. A creature that takes damage from the spell is [blinded](/Conditions.aspx?ID=59) for 1 round and [dazzled](/Conditions.aspx?ID=65) for a number of rounds equal to the spell level. On a critical success on the attack roll, the target is also blinded for as long as it’s dazzled from the spell. However, it can attempt a Fortitude saving throw against your spell DC at the end of each of its turns, ending the blinded condition on a success (but remaining dazzled).

**Craft Requirements** Supply a casting of [_searing light_](/Spells.aspx?ID=269) of the appropriate level.

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Treasure Vault (Remastered)](/Sources.aspx?ID=191) pg. 139

<row gap="medium">

**Usage** held in 1 hand

**Bulk** L
</row>

<row gap="medium">

 

 

 
</row>

</column>

---

Carvings of skulls, monsters, and all manner of violence decorate this wand of blackened bone, but it makes absurd sounds when Activated, such as a honking horn, a manic giggle, or a daydreamy sigh.

**Activate** <actions string="" /> Cast a Spell;  **Frequency** once per day, plus overcharge;   **Effect** You cast [_impending doom_](/Spells.aspx?ID=929) of the indicated rank, showing the target a potential death that's gruesome and absurd. If the target becomes [frightened](/Conditions.aspx?ID=19) by the spell, it also becomes [stupefied](/Conditions.aspx?ID=37) with a value 1 higher than the frightened value. This lasts for the duration of the spell.

**Craft Requirements** Supply a casting of _impending doom_ of the appropriate rank.

Carvings of skulls, monsters, and all manner of violence decorate this wand of blackened bone, but it makes absurd sounds when Activated, such as a honking horn, a manic giggle, or a daydreamy sigh.

**Activate** <actions string="" /> Cast a Spell;  **Frequency** once per day, plus overcharge;   **Effect** You cast [_impending doom_](/Spells.aspx?ID=929) of the indicated level, showing the target a potential death that’s gruesome and absurd. This lasts for the duration of the spell.

**Craft Requirements** Supply a casting of [_impending doom_](/Spells.aspx?ID=929) of the appropriate level.

**Activate** <actions string="" /> Cast a Spell;  **Frequency** once per day, plus overcharge;   **Effect** You cast [_impending doom_](/Spells.aspx?ID=929) of the indicated rank, showing the target a potential death that's gruesome and absurd. If the target becomes [frightened](/Conditions.aspx?ID=19) by the spell, it also becomes [stupefied](/Conditions.aspx?ID=37) with a value 1 higher than the frightened value. This lasts for the duration of the spell.

**Craft Requirements** Supply a casting of _impending doom_ of the appropriate rank.

Carvings of skulls, monsters, and all manner of violence decorate this wand of blackened bone, but it makes absurd sounds when Activated, such as a honking horn, a manic giggle, or a daydreamy sigh.

**Activate** <actions string="" /> Cast a Spell;  **Frequency** once per day, plus overcharge;   **Effect** You cast [_impending doom_](/Spells.aspx?ID=929) of the indicated rank, showing the target a potential death that's gruesome and absurd. If the target becomes [frightened](/Conditions.aspx?ID=19) by the spell, it also becomes [stupefied](/Conditions.aspx?ID=37) with a value 1 higher than the frightened value. This lasts for the duration of the spell.

**Craft Requirements** Supply a casting of _impending doom_ of the appropriate rank.

[Wand of Dumbfounding Doom](/Equipment.aspx?ID=2278)
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Emotion" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=60" />
<trait label="Fear" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=68" />
<trait label="Incapacitation" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=93" />
<trait label="Magical" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=103" />
<trait label="Mental" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=106" />
<trait label="Prediction" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=132" />
<trait label="Wand" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=164" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Treasure Vault (Remastered)](/Sources.aspx?ID=191) pg. 139

<row gap="medium">

**Usage** held in 1 hand

**Bulk** L
</row>

<row gap="medium">

 

 

 
</row>

</column>

---

Carvings of skulls, monsters, and all manner of violence decorate this wand of blackened bone, but it makes absurd sounds when Activated, such as a honking horn, a manic giggle, or a daydreamy sigh.

**Activate** <actions string="" /> Cast a Spell;  **Frequency** once per day, plus overcharge;   **Effect** You cast [_impending doom_](/Spells.aspx?ID=929) of the indicated rank, showing the target a potential death that's gruesome and absurd. If the target becomes [frightened](/Conditions.aspx?ID=19) by the spell, it also becomes [stupefied](/Conditions.aspx?ID=37) with a value 1 higher than the frightened value. This lasts for the duration of the spell.

**Craft Requirements** Supply a casting of _impending doom_ of the appropriate rank.

fields.text: Item 8+ Wand of Dumbfounding Doom Emotion Fear Incapacitation Magical Mental Prediction Wand Source Treasure Vault (Remastered) pg. 139 Usage held in 1 hand Bulk L Carvings of skulls, monsters, and all manner of violence decorate this wand of blackened bone, but it makes absurd sounds when Activated, such as a honking horn, a manic giggle, or a daydreamy sigh. Activate Cast a Spell; Frequency once per day, plus overcharge; Effect You cast impending doom of the indicated rank, showing the target a potential death that's gruesome and absurd. If the target becomes frightened by the spell, it also becomes stupefied with a value 1 higher than the frightened value. This lasts for the duration of the spell. Craft Requirements Supply a casting of impending doom of the appropriate rank. >
[Wand of Fey Flames](/Equipment.aspx?ID=1377)
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Uncommon" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=159" />
<trait label="Evocation" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=65" />
<trait label="Light" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=100" />
<trait label="Magical" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=103" />
<trait label="Wand" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=164" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Grand Bazaar](/Sources.aspx?ID=100) pg. 81

**Price** 360 gp

<row gap="medium">

**Usage** held in 1 hand

**Bulk** L
</row>

<row gap="medium">

 

 

 
</row>

</column>

---

This red maple wand carved into a tongue of flame feels warm in your hand.

**Activate** <actions string="" /> Cast a Spell;  **Frequency** once per day, plus overcharge;   **Effect** You cast [_faerie fire_](/Spells.aspx?ID=107). For the duration of the spell, you can use the limning flames as a source for your magic. Creatures affected by your _faerie fire_ must succeed at a Will save against your spell DC or take a –2 status penalty to their Will saves against [enchantment](/Traits.aspx?ID=61) and [illusions](/Traits.aspx?ID=92) spells as long as they are affected by _faerie fire_. You can cast an enchantment or illusion spell on such a creature up to a distance twice the spell's normal range. If the spell has a range of touch, or doesn't have a range, it is unaffected by the increase in range from the _faerie fire_.

**Craft Requirements** Supply a casting of _faerie fire_.

<column gap="tiny">

</column>

<row gap="medium">

**Usage** held in 1 hand

**Bulk** L
</row>

<row gap="medium">

 

 

 
</row>

</column>

---

Carved from a hawthorn branch, this wand has a smooth handle, but the shaft remains covered in bark and long thorns. Polished red stones, arranged like a cluster of berries, decorate the pommel.

**Activate** <actions string="" /> Cast a Spell;  **Frequency** once per day, plus overcharge;   **Effect** You cast [_oaken resilience_](/Spells.aspx?ID=1617) of the indicated rank, and the target sprouts long thorns like those of a hawthorn tree. While _oaken resilience_ lasts, any creature that hits the target with an unarmed Strike or otherwise touches it takes piercing damage from the thorns, with the amount determined by the wand’s type. A creature that has [engulfed](/MonsterAbilities.aspx?ID=61) or [swallowed](/MonsterAbilities.aspx?ID=77) the target takes this damage as well at the start of each of the target’s turns.

**Craft Requirements** Supply a casting of _Oaken Resilience_ of the appropriate rank.

</column>

**Source** [Treasure Vault](/Sources.aspx?ID=320) pg. 140

<row gap="medium">

**Usage** held in 1 hand

**Bulk** L
</row>

<row gap="medium">

 

 

 
</row>

</column>

---

Carved from a hawthorn branch, this wand has a smooth handle, but the shaft remains covered in bark and long thorns. Polished red stones, arranged like a cluster of berries, decorate the pommel.

**Activate** <actions string="" /> Cast a Spell;  **Frequency** once per day, plus overcharge;   **Effect** You cast [_barkskin_](/Spells.aspx?ID=20) of the indicated level, and the target sprouts long thorns like those of a hawthorn tree. While barkskin lasts, any creature that hits the target with an unarmed Strike or otherwise touches it takes piercing damage from the thorns, with the amount determined by the wand's type. A creature that has [engulfed](/MonsterAbilities.aspx?ID=61) or [swallowed](/MonsterAbilities.aspx?ID=77) the target takes this damage as well at the start of each of the target's turns.

**Craft Requirements** Supply a casting of [_barkskin_](/Spells.aspx?ID=20) of the appropriate level.

</column>

Carved from a hawthorn branch, this wand has a smooth handle, but the shaft remains covered in bark and long thorns. Polished red stones, arranged like a cluster of berries, decorate the pommel.

**Activate** <actions string="" /> Cast a Spell;  **Frequency** once per day, plus overcharge;   **Effect** You cast [_oaken resilience_](/Spells.aspx?ID=1617) of the indicated rank, and the target sprouts long thorns like those of a hawthorn tree. While _oaken resilience_ lasts, any creature that hits the target with an unarmed Strike or otherwise touches it takes piercing damage from the thorns, with the amount determined by the wand’s type. A creature that has [engulfed](/MonsterAbilities.aspx?ID=61) or [swallowed](/MonsterAbilities.aspx?ID=77) the target takes this damage as well at the start of each of the target’s turns.

**Craft Requirements** Supply a casting of _Oaken Resilience_ of the appropriate rank.

The grain of this simple wooden wand forms shifting images of sharp claws, snapping jaws, and countless creatures.

**Activate** <actions string="" /> Cast a Spell; This activation takes <actions string="Two Actions" /> if the spell normally takes <actions string="Single Action" /> to cast, or <actions string="Three Actions" /> if the spell normally takes <actions string="Two Actions" />;  **Frequency** once per day, plus overcharge;   **Effect** You Cast the Spell, selecting two forms from among those you can normally choose. You gain the benefits of both forms. For example, if one form can breathe air and the other can breathe underwater, you can breathe in both situations. If there's overlap in abilities, you gain the better one. For instance, if both have a fly Speed, you get the higher one, and if both forms have claws, you gain only the claw Strike you prefer. The GM determines which abilities overlap and which are cumulative.

**Craft Requirements** Supply a casting of a spell of the appropriate rank. The spell must have a casting time of <actions string="Single Action" /> or <actions string="Two Actions" />, must have the [polymorph](/Traits.aspx?ID=127) trait, and must allow more than one choice of battle form.

You gain the benefits of both forms. For example, if one form can breathe air and the other can breathe underwater, you can breathe in both situations. If there's overlap in abilities, you gain the better one. For instance, if both have a fly Speed, you get the higher one, and if both forms have claws, you gain only the claw Strike you prefer. <row gap="medium">

**Usage** held in 1 hand

**Bulk** L
</row>

<row gap="medium">

 

 

 
</row>

</column>

---

The grain of this simple wooden wand forms shifting images of sharp claws, snapping jaws, and countless creatures.

**Activate** <actions string="" /> Cast a Spell; This activation takes <actions string="Two Actions" /> if the spell normally takes <actions string="Single Action" /> to cast, or <actions string="Three Actions" /> if the spell normally takes <actions string="Two Actions" />;  **Frequency** once per day, plus overcharge;   **Effect** You Cast the Spell, selecting two forms from among those you can normally choose. You gain the benefits of both forms. For example, if one form can breathe air and the other can breathe underwater, you can breathe in both situations. If there's overlap in abilities, you gain the better one. For instance, if both have a fly Speed, you get the higher one, and if both forms have claws, you gain only the claw Strike you prefer. The GM determines which abilities overlap and which are cumulative.

**Craft Requirements** Supply a casting of a spell of the appropriate rank. The spell must have a casting time of <actions string="Single Action" /> or <actions string="Two Actions" />, must have the [polymorph](/Traits.aspx?ID=127) trait, and must allow more than one choice of battle form.

---

The grain of this simple wooden wand forms shifting images of sharp claws, snapping jaws, and countless creatures.

**Activate** <actions string="" /> Cast a Spell; This activation takes <actions string="Two Actions" /> if the spell normally takes <actions string="Single Action" /> to cast, or <actions string="Three Actions" /> if the spell normally takes <actions string="Two Actions" />;  **Frequency** once per day, plus overcharge;   **Effect** You Cast the Spell, selecting two forms from among those you can normally choose. You gain the benefits of both forms. For example, if one form can breathe air and the other can breathe underwater, you can breathe in both situations. If there’s overlap in abilities, you gain the better one. For instance, if both have a [fly Speed](/Rules.aspx?ID=2350), you get the higher one, and if both forms have claws, you gain only the claw Strike you prefer. The GM determines which abilities overlap and which are cumulative.

**Craft Requirements** Supply a casting of a spell of the appropriate level. The spell must have a casting time of <actions string="Single Action" /> or <actions string="Two Actions" />, must have the [polymorph](/Traits.aspx?ID=670) trait, and must allow more than one choice of battle form.

>
[Wand of Legerdemain](/Equipment.aspx?ID=2281)
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Magical" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=103" />
<trait label="Wand" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=164" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Treasure Vault (Remastered)](/Sources.aspx?ID=191) pg. 140

<row gap="medium">

**Usage** held in 1 hand

**Bulk** L
</row>

<row gap="medium">

 

 

 
</row>

</column>

---

This wand of lacquered black wood has a handle wrapped in interwoven colorful ribbons. A silver bell caps the wand's tasseled pommel.

**Activate** <actions string="" /> Cast a Spell;  **Frequency** once per day, plus overcharge;   **Effect** You Cast the Spell.

**Activate** <actions string="Single Action" /> Interact ([emotion](/Traits.aspx?ID=60), [illusion](/Traits.aspx?ID=92), [light](/Traits.aspx?ID=100), [mental](/Traits.aspx?ID=106), [visual](/Traits.aspx?ID=163))   **Requirements** The last action you took this turn was to Cast a Spell from the wand; **Effect** You make yourself the center of attention. An illusory spotlight shines [bright light](/Rules.aspx?ID=407) upon your space as you pull inane objects from the wand's tip, such as confetti, silk flowers, streamers, or a long string of colorful kerchiefs knotted end to end. Each enemy within 30 feet must attempt a Will save against your spell DC, receiving a +4 circumstance bonus to the save if you or any of your allies recently threatened it or used [hostile actions](/Rules.aspx?ID=300) against it. On a failure, the creature becomes [fascinated](/Conditions.aspx?ID=14) with you until the end of your next turn. The fascination ends if the target is subject to a hostile act, or if another creature succeeds at a [Diplomacy](/Skills.aspx?ID=6) or [Intimidation](/Skills.aspx?ID=7) check against it.

 The spotlight follows you wherever you move. You can't be [concealed](/Conditions.aspx?ID=4) while in the spotlight. The effect ends if you become [invisible](/Conditions.aspx?ID=26), attempt a [Stealth](/Skills.aspx?ID=15) check, or Dismiss the activation.

 You can Sustain this Activation for up to 1 minute. Since you need to keep performing tricks, Sustain an Activation has the [manipulate](/Traits.aspx?ID=104) trait. Sustaining extends the spotlight, and keeps fascinated creatures fascinated, but doesn't cause creatures not already fascinated to become fascinated.

**Craft Requirements** Supply a casting of a spell of the appropriate rank.
